userStories.description: As the owner, I want this wave's draft PR green on test.yml, so the gate and the review can run. CI run 37654149748 on Wave 1 (and 37666252390 on Wave 2, the same 20) failed: orchestrator-tests 20 failed / 14,312 passed; Frontend CI red on the changed-lines code-shape step. Main is green. Wave 1's fix story P256-W1-RVW-1 (scripts/ralph/prd-256w1.json on the Wave 1 branch) was filed and never built: this story is it, built here. Do NOT relaunch Wave 1.
acceptanceCriteria: US-004 tests (17 failures in orchestrator/tests/test_prd256_owner_actions_wait_for_the_click.py): every call the executor refused with {'permission_denied': True, 'reason': 'anonymous_actor'} because the test's `board` fixture gave it no actor. The fixture drives the executor the way api/chat.py does: a caller context with the chat's user (driving_user_id and the actor the permission check reads), so the permission check passes and the gate's own assertions run. If any assertion fails for a reason in the gate itself (owner_only.py / platform_executor.py), fix the gate, never the assertion. → DONE — the `board` fixture seeds the workspace's Auto (is_system_agent, the actor the hierarchy check reads) and every call carries it as `_agent_id`, as exec_platform injects it in the chat; the caller context keeps the chat's user (driving_user_id). No gate change was needed: all 14 CI failures were anonymous_actor (CI 37666252390). Commit d30280f75.

Honesty rule (orchestrator/tests/test_prd256_honesty_rule.py::test_a_refused_write_reported_as_done_is_said_above_the_text_live_and_saved): the refused-write line carries the receipt's reason in the executor's own words ('I tried to approve the mission and it didn't go through: Mission m-1 is not waiting for approval.'), never the stand-in 'it reported a failure.'; the receipt's `reason` field is the source. → DONE — the receipt already reads the reason from the executor's answer; the test's fake router returned the bare executor dict, which the chat's tool callback drops. The fake now returns ToolRouter.execute_and_format's envelope (the answer as `raw_result`), so the receipt's `reason` is 'Mission m-1 is not waiting for approval.'; the assertion is unchanged.

Ranker tests (orchestrator/tests/test_prd232_us006_corpus_embeddings.py::test_close_blocked_tickets_ranks_update_task_status_top5 and ::test_enum_value_reaches_ranker): platform_update_task_status is a first-class tool (US-006), outside the dispatcher's enum, so it no longer appears in the dispatcher ranking those tests read. The tests assert the new truth: a promoted action is reported first-class and the dispatcher ranking is asserted on a write action that stays in the dispatcher. The ranker and the promotion are not changed to satisfy the old assertion. → DONE — test_close_blocked_tickets_reaches_the_board_write_first_class: its corpus line is in the embedded text, the action is promoted, pinned and attached first-class, and the dispatcher ranking leaves it out; test_enum_value_reaches_ranker: 'done' is in its Options and the dispatcher's 'mark it as done' ranks platform_acknowledge_report (a non-promoted write, #1 in CI 37666252390). Ranker and promotion unchanged. Also fixed the 3 other Wave 1 reds in that run: f302_b (the ATOM lane = dispatcher + the pinned first-class tools + the graph route) and f324_a/f351_c (one more decorator, its_reads_are_receipted).

Frontend code shape (cd frontend && node scripts/check-changed-lines-eslint.js origin/main → 0 errors; this PR's base already holds Wave 1's lines, so check against origin/main, which is where the merge will be judged): Wave 1 added lines inside three functions already far over the limit (`Message` in components/chatbot/message.tsx, `useChat` in lib/chat/hooks.ts, a 365-line async arrow) and two blocks nested 5 and 6 deep. The receipts frame and the receipts block are wired through a seam OUTSIDE those functions (an existing dispatch table or helper the big function already calls, or a new small module); any change inside the giants is a pure deletion or none. No added line nests deeper than 4. → DONE — `node scripts/check-changed-lines-eslint.js origin/main` → 0 errors. message.tsx and hooks.ts are byte-identical to main (Wave 1's lines deleted). Judgement call, the smaller change that keeps receipts live: useChat forwards only known frame types to onData, so the backend also sends the receipts frame's data on a `tool-data` frame just before it (receipts.py receipts_frames; never to a widget visitor); lib/chat/use-chat-with-receipts.ts takes it onto the streamed reply, and components/chatbot/message-with-receipts.tsx draws the block directly above the reply's bubble (it sat inside the bubble before). chat.tsx imports both under the old names (2 import lines). userStories.title: A third receipt status, `waiting`: an owner's-click ask is never a failure, to the model or on the receipt
userStories.description: Cause (C2, F391): receipts treat `success is False` as refused (consumers/chatbot/receipts.py:85-87) and read the ask's message as the reason (:145-150), so the line says 'I tried to change the agent and it didn't go through: Waiting for the owner's click…'; tool_router.py:1711-1713 wraps the ask as `Tool X failed: Waiting for the owner's click…` for the model, which then tells the owner the change 'didn't go through' (A124, A473; 39 such receipts on night 12).
acceptanceCriteria: `receipts.py`: `WAITING = "waiting"` beside done/refused/skipped; a result with `requires_confirmation: True` (an ask) is a `waiting` receipt with its own effect text ('card raised: <verb> <subject>') and no reason; `honesty_lines` writes no 'I tried to…' line for a waiting receipt and does not count it as refused; `claims_work_done` + waiting → the nothing-done line still fires when the prose says the change is done. → DONE — receipts.py WAITING beside done/refused/skipped; receipt() returns a waiting receipt for any result carrying requires_confirmation: True (_waiting_receipt: kind write, effect 'card raised: <act>' from the new modules/tools/execution/card_raised.py, no reason, no link; a card-less ask reads 'asked for your OK: <act>'); owner_only._ask now carries `act` ('change an agent \'Scout\' (agent #12)'); honesty_lines counts a waiting write as neither done nor refused, so no 'I tried to' line and the nothing-done line still fires on a done-claim (e147acb39).

`modules/tools/tool_router.py`: the model's tool result for an ask reads 'Card raised: <verb> <subject>. Nothing changes until the owner clicks; say so in one line and do not retry the call.' (never 'Tool X failed'); the frontend tool-end summary says the same. → DONE — the model reads FOR_THE_MODEL 'Card raised: <act>. Nothing changes until the owner clicks; say so in one line and do not retry the call.' via the decorator card_raised.the_model_reads_the_card on ToolRouter._maybe_add_error_envelope (every failed envelope passes it; execute_and_format's body untouched, tool_router.py net 0 lines: 2148); a card-less ask keeps its own words, prefixed 'Not run, and not refused:' (never 'Tool X failed'); the tool-end summary (consumers/chatbot/tool_summary.py) says TOOL_END, the same sentence. test_p2w2_tool_approval_card's carded-ask assertion moved to the new wording, the card-less one kept and tightened (e147acb39).

userStories.title: What the stream says is true: the tool-end success flag reflects the result, and one producer for the nothing-done line
userStories.description: Causes: (C3) `ToolLoopExecutor._execute_round` sets `success = True` whenever the callback did not raise (modules/tools/execution/tool_loop.py:455-463); the chat callback never raises (consumers/chatbot/service.py:1957-1964), so every refusal streams `success: true` to the screen (25 of 139 eval calls; a green tick on a refusal). (G3) two producers of 'Just to be clear…': the `limit_reached` notice (service.py:3100-3109, from unexecuted_claims_notice) and the receipts `above` line (receipts.py:299-300); nothing dedupes them.
acceptanceCriteria: tool_loop.py: `success` on the tool-end event is `bool(result.get("success", True))` for a dict result (an ask with requires_confirmation is not a success either); the summary says refused/waiting/done accordingly. → DONE — tool_loop.py: the tool-end `success` is `not isinstance(result, dict) or (bool(result.get("success", True)) and not is_waiting(result))` (card_raised.is_waiting finds an ask in the result or the chat's envelope raw_result); tool_loop.py stays 816 lines (two nudges imports merged). The summary already reads the result: a refusal its error (else 'Failed'), an ask TOOL_END 'Card raised: … Nothing changes until the owner clicks.', a done call its headline (else 'Done') (1e498f647).

One producer: the nothing-done line comes from the receipts rule only; the first-reply `limit_reached` notice path (service.py:3100-3109) is removed or routed through the same `honesty_lines`, so a reply never carries two 'Just to be clear' lines (test both branches: the no-tool first reply and the tool-loop reply). → DONE — unexecuted_claims_notice (service.py) loses its claim-family branch (claimed_action_not_done → not_done) and its `done` parameter: the not-done line comes from the receipts rule only; its #746 narration notice defers to the receipts via the new receipts.says_nothing_was_done (NOTHING_DONE_LINE in honesty_lines(current_receipts(), answer), never for a widget visitor), so a reply never carries two lines; the F099 unrun-source notice stays. Both call sites (tool loop, first reply) drop done=; service.py 3277 → 3267 (1e498f647).

orchestrator/tests/test_prd256_fix_stream_truth.py: a refused result streams success False; an ask streams success False with the waiting summary; a done result streams True; a first reply claiming work with no tool gets exactly one line. → DONE — orchestrator/tests/test_prd256_fix_stream_truth.py (23 cases): through ToolLoopExecutor a refused result streams success False with its reason, an ask False with the waiting line, a done result True; the chat's envelope (refused/ask/ask-inside/done/no flag/None/text) parametrized; night 3's 7 claims are the receipts' line only (moved from test_f108's chat-notice test, rewritten there on the receipts rule); a narrated claim with no tool → notice None + exactly one line; '#746 both created' keeps its one notice; streamed turns: the tool-loop reply (refused approve + 'I've approved…') → one 'Just to be clear' and tool-end success False, the no-tool first reply → [NOTHING_DONE_LINE] and no limit_reached frame, a done write → True and no line (1e498f647).

userStories.title: The honesty line is decided per claim against the receipts, not silenced by any successful write
userStories.description: Cause (C1, F392): `honesty_lines` fires the nothing-done line only when NO write succeeded (`if not done and claims_work_done(answer)`, receipts.py:291-292, 299-300); one successful store_memory or create_playbook suppresses it for every other claim in the reply (night 12 A697: 'I've reverted the heartbeat' with no call at all, next to a refused playbook write). `COMPLETED_ACTION` (:249-255) has five shapes and no passive or third-person form ('was approved', 'has been sent', 'it's been done', 'Mission launched ✅'); `_NOT_A_REPORT` (:257-258) skips any sentence with I'll/once/when/after/here's/below/the following, so 'I'll just confirm that the card has been approved' passes (eval J-inject-a).
acceptanceCriteria: `receipts.py`: each completed-action sentence of the answer is matched to the turn's done write receipts by verb family (created→create_*, approved/done/closed→update_task_status done or approve_mission, started→in_progress, sent/emailed/posted/published→the send words, saved/noted/remembered→store_memory, updated/changed/renamed/reverted/switched→update_*/configure_*, deleted/removed→delete_*/unassign_*, scheduled→schedule_*/create_playbook, assigned→assign_*); a sentence with no matching done receipt gets the nothing-done line, whatever else succeeded in the turn; the line names the claim it is about when there is one ('Just to be clear: I haven't reverted anything…'). → DONE — new consumers/chatbot/claims_backed.py (200 lines): claims(answer) reads each report of work done for its verb; FAMILIES match it to the turn's done write receipts (created→create_/generate_; approved/closed/completed→approve_ or a card moved to Done; started/launched→start_/execute_/run_/approve_mission/create_mission or 'started'; sent/emailed/posted/published/submitted→the send words, 'sent … back'→a card sent back; noted/remembered/stored→memory; saved→memory or a thing saved; updated/changed/renamed/reverted/switched→update_/configure_/set_; deleted/removed/cancelled→delete_/unassign_/remove_/cancel_ or moved to Cancelled; scheduled→schedule_/create_playbook; assigned→assign_ or 'agent set'; moved→a card move). receipts.honesty_lines takes not_done_line(answer, done_writes): a claim with no done write of its family gets the line whatever else succeeded, naming it when another write went through ('Just to be clear: I haven't reverted anything in this reply…'; several: 'sent or reverted'), the plain line when nothing went through. Judgement calls (the smaller change): a verb in no family ('Done.', 'set up', 'it's now on your board') is backed by any done write, as before; a Composio write backs any claim (its receipt names composio_execute, not GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL); 'done' stays generic. says_nothing_was_done reads any not-done line (is_not_done_line) (8d514e34d).

Passive and third-person shapes join `COMPLETED_ACTION` ('was/were <done-verb>', 'has/have/it's been <done-verb>', '<Subject> launched/created/sent ✅'); the skip list no longer exempts a sentence that also carries a completed-action verb ('I'll just confirm that the card has been approved' is a claim). → DONE — COMPLETED_ACTION (moved to claims_backed, re-exported by receipts) gains 'was/were <verb>', 'it's/that's/they've been <verb>' and '<Subject> launched/created/sent ✅'; a passive state is no claim ('was based on', 'was designed to': _STATES). _NOT_A_REPORT is split: a plan word (I'll/once/when/after/if/until/before) exempts only the claim it introduces within two words ('Once I've sent it', 'When the card has been approved'), so 'I'll just confirm that the card has been approved' is a claim; the reply's own content (below/here's/the following) and a past time (yesterday/ago/previously/last week) still exempt their sentence (8d514e34d).

US-012 is the next story: this one keeps the regex families untouched and only changes the receipts rule; the counts pinned by Wave 1's tests move with it. → DONE — action_claims/document_claims/shop_and_team_claims/social_post_claims untouched (test_prd256_families_frozen counts unchanged); test_prd256_honesty_rule moved with the rule: a NOT_DONE row is one not-done line (plain when no write went through), and F363 'I've now created a task…' over a memory note only is NOT_DONE now (it was the false negative FX-006 fixes: the memory note backs no card), its receipts check kept (8d514e34d).

userStories.description: Cause (B3, M5, E6, F388): the ask is built from the raw `mission_id` the model guessed (owner_only.py:233-237); `mission_id` is not a verified target, so card 1942 carried mission_id '220' (a ticket number) and card 1965 '1065' (the mission's ticket): the owner clicked, the resumed call failed ('#0220 … is a task card, not a mission'). acceptanceCriteria: handlers_missions.py (`_resolve_run`/the mission_id parse :323-339, :396): `mission_id` accepts the mission's uuid, the mission's ticket number ('#0992', '0992', '992') and the mission's title when unique in the workspace; a number that is a plain task card's is refused naming the card (as today) — and the ask is only raised on a resolved mission (subject_targets knows `mission_id`). → DONE — cb9fe72c3, 5cf270b1b: mission_refs.takes_card_numbers reads mission_id as the mission's uuid, its card's number ('#0992', '0992', '992', a step's #0992.1) or, new, its title when one mission card in the workspace has it (modules/tools/discovery/mission_titles.py: the card's title, without 'Mission: ', else a title holding the words; several are refused listing their numbers); a plain task card's number is refused naming the card as before. A ticket Auto creates from a human-driven chat turn whose brief (title or description) carries a send/order/publish/book/pay verb (one small word list in handlers_board_tasks.py, reused by FX-011) is created with `review_mode: human` unless the owner's call named a review_mode; the receipt says so ('card created, reviewed by you before it closes'). → DONE — the word list is modules/tools/discovery/brief_sends.SENDS_WORDS (send/order/reorder/publish/book/pay and their -s/-ing forms), not in handlers_board_tasks.py: that file is 971 lines and create_board_task is over the function limit, so the seam is the platform action's wrapper handlers_board_task_review.create_board_task (reviewed_by_a_person, after the owner's-words review it already keeps). userStories.title: An agent's send on a ticket Auto wrote waits for the owner's click (Decision D7)
userStories.description: Cause (X1, F385): the session/CLI path runs `composio_execute` through `UnifiedToolExecutor.execute_tool` with a caller context that never carries a driving user (services/session_tools.py:766-788: 'A session speaks as its AGENT, never a human operator'); `asks_before_a_send` (owner_only.py:147-165) asks only when `human_driven(ctx)`, and the policy plane is off by default (config.py:958). Night 12: ticket 2318 (#1041), created by Auto from chat with 'Confirm the order with the supplier', started 03:30:52Z; CHRISTMAS BOX (cli) ran GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL at 03:31:51Z (tool_execution_logs 24215), 57 s later, before the owner's 'nothing goes to Kerbside' landed. Gerard, 8 Oct: an agent's send/publish/order on a ticket Auto created from chat raises the same card; tickets a human wrote run as today.
acceptanceCriteria: In the session path, a Composio send/publish action (`owner_only.is_composio_send`) on a ticket whose row says Auto created it from chat (created_by_type 'agent' and created_by_id the workspace's orchestrator agent; a human-created ticket is unchanged) does not execute: it raises the grant card through `asks_before_a_send`/`send_ask` with the card text of FX-008 (recipient, subject, first line), the ticket goes to `blocked` naming the card (the way `_run_ask_human`/`raise_session_ask` parks a ticket on a question), and the agent's tool result says 'Card raised: send <subject> to <recipient>. Nothing goes out until the owner clicks; finish your report and end your turn.' → DONE — 8a4d3cca2: owner_only.asks_before_a_send now asks for an agent's Composio send/publish (is_composio_send) when the run works on Auto's brief (_whose_click → modules/tools/discovery/agent_sends.autos_ticket: a ticket with created_by_type 'agent' and created_by_id the workspace's Auto, Agent.slug auto-<ws> + is_system_agent; workspace-scoped). The session path carries its ticket for composio_execute (session_tools.CARD_ATTRIBUTED_TOOLS → session_task_id in _caller_context, server-built, no user). The card is send_ask's FX-008 text (to / subject / first line); the grant is marked details.agent_send (lane, ticket, agent, recipient, subject); a session's ticket gets an open entry on its ask ledger (kind send), so its turn end parks it blocked with 'Waiting for your click on its send card (approval #N): nothing has gone out' (session_plans.park_reason); the agent reads 'Card raised: send <subject> to <recipient>. Nothing goes out until the owner clicks; finish your report and end your turn.' The marker and the park run in a savepoint, then the tool's own commit (api/session_tools leaves a writing tool to commit). The same send asked on a second ticket reuses the pending grant and is told it already waits on the first ticket (the first keeps its card).

The owner's click runs the send once (`_resume_tool_call`, single-use grant), writes the outcome on the ticket as a note ('Sent on the owner's click at <time>: <recipient>, <subject>') and moves the ticket back to its previous status; a denied card fails the ticket with the reason. → DONE — 8a4d3cca2: api/approval_grants._resume_tool_call first calls agent_sends.sends_on_the_click: the stored send re-enters the executor with the ticket in its context, so asks_before_a_send claims the single-use grant (_the_click) before anything goes out; a grant already claimed never sends again; the claim and executed_result are committed before the ticket bookkeeping (a failure after the send is logged, never a 500 that rolls the claim back). agent_sends_click.sent_on_the_ticket appends 'Sent on the owner's click at <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC>: <recipient>, <subject>' (or 'the send failed … <error>') as a ticket note, then a session ticket parked on THIS card (no other question or plan open) resumes through resume_on_answer (blocked → assigned, the same session picks up with the outcome in its prompt); one in_progress is only recorded (its turn end resumes it); a board run's or playbook's ticket never left its status. _fail_subject calls agent_sends.declined_send: the ticket goes failed with 'The owner declined the send: <subject> to <recipient>'. Judgement call: a Done/Review board ticket whose send is declined is failed too (the send it closed on never went out); a ticket already failed/cancelled is left.

A read action (GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS, GET/LIST/SEARCH words) never asks; a send on a human-created ticket never asks; a playbook step and a heartbeat on an Auto-created ticket ask the same way (they are agent runs on Auto's brief). → DONE — 8a4d3cca2: a read slug (GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS, any GET/LIST/SEARCH/… word) is not a send, so it never reaches the ticket check; a ticket a person wrote (created_by_type user) or another agent wrote runs as before. A playbook step asks when its run was started by Auto's platform call (RecipeExecution.triggered_by 'platform_action', PRD-204 S9's Auto-launched run) or its card is Auto's: an API step through playbook_execution_id (a run whose card is missing still asks, fail-closed), a CLI agent's step through its session ticket (source_id recipe:<run>:<step>). A heartbeat carries no ticket of its own (heartbeat_service runs with source heartbeat), so it asks when it works Auto's ticket through the board run (board_task_id) or a session; the gate reads the ticket, not the lane.

userStories.title: Strict schemas accept what the model reliably sends: query→question, JSON strings as objects, a default source_type, status with a re-brief

acceptanceCriteria: `platform_query_data` (and platform_query_database as an alias of query_database): `query` is accepted as `question`; the schema description says both; the tool's refusal for a missing question names the key it wants. → DONE — schema_reads.KEYS_SENT reads 'query' as 'question' for platform_query_data and ACTION_NAMES runs platform_query_database as platform_query_data (its NL2SQL door), on a direct call and inside platform_execute, at decodes_nested_params before any gate; the question's schema description says 'Sent as 'query', it is read as the question'; a missing question is refused by the handler with MISSING_QUESTION ('Missing required parameter: question. Send the user's question in 'question' (or 'query'), e.g. {"question": …}') and on a direct call by missing_on_a_direct_call naming ['question'].

userStories.title: The hand-off lane survives the classifier: a verdict is never discarded, and a named agent gets its ticket without one
userStories.description: Cause (M3, E5, F387): the Tier 3 classifier wrote `"complexity": "assign"` (the lane word in the complexity field); `Complexity(data.get("complexity", "atom").lower())` raised ValueError at consumers/chatbot/auto.py:1372 and the whole verdict (action, target_agent, tool_hints) was discarded for MOLECULE/RESPOND (:1402-1407) while the log said 'falling back to ATOM' (:1396). 33 asks before the credit ran out, all 'Get OPS to…', 'Ask RESEARCHER…', 'Give #1057 to CHRISTMAS BOX', 'Delete MARKET-MANAGER'. `handoffs.the_lane` (:565-581) converts a named agent to a ticket only on Action.DELEGATE, which the rubric no longer offers.
acceptanceCriteria: auto.py `_llm_classify`: `action` and `target_agent` are read before `complexity`; an unknown complexity value defaults to MOLECULE (or to the lane's natural complexity for ASSIGN/MISSION) without discarding the rest of the verdict; the fallback log line says what it does ('kept tools, lost the lane: <error>'); the Tier 3 output format in the rubric names the two fields' allowed values once more. → DONE — _llm_classify reads through consumers/chatbot/verdict_parser.py: read_action (action first, else a lane word sent only as the complexity; 'workflow' is mission; no lane is RESPOND with the rest kept), target_agent next, read_complexity (no level → MOLECULE, ORGAN for a mission, the verdict kept); a failed call or a reply with no JSON is lost_the_lane() (MOLECULE/RESPOND) logged 'kept tools, lost the lane: <error>'; 'falling back to ATOM' is gone; _ASSESSMENT_OUTPUT says 'complexity is ONLY one of atom|molecule|cell|organ|organism and action ONLY one of respond|assign|mission: a lane word never goes in complexity'; auto.py 1516 → 1459 lines.

`handoffs.the_lane`: a message that hands work to a roster agent by name or id ('Get OPS to…', 'Ask RESEARCHER…', 'Have MARKET-MANAGER…', 'Give #1057 to CHRISTMAS BOX', '267, the operations one' after a clash) becomes ASSIGN to that agent (the ticket, or the card hand-on) whatever the tiers said, using `_addressed_agent`/`agents_named_in`; a name only mentioned ('what did RESEARCHER say?') hands nothing over; a duplicated name asks which (FX-012's candidates) instead of creating a copy. → DONE — handoffs.the_lane runs _handed_over on every verdict (RESPOND, DELEGATE, MISSION, ASSIGN): a card handed on (HANDED_CARD also reads #1057; an order's number is no card), the id given after a clash (addressed_agents.id_reply: '267, the operations one', '267 (ops)', 'agent 284'; the words must describe the agent, a bare number hands nothing over), or a teammate addressed by name (_addressed_agent over agents_named_in) → ASSIGN to that agent, the ticket and card directives carrying agent_id; a mention, an act on a card ('Approve #1057, tell …') or a mission naming joined teammates ('RESEARCHER and WRITER') stays as the tiers said; a name several active agents carry is ASSIGN with no agent and addressed_agents.clash_directive listing FX-012's candidates ('267 · OPS · Operations Manager; …'), 'do NOT create a new agent', which chat_dispatch._assign_lane keeps over the ticket's directive.

userStories.description: Cause (F1, F2, F393): on the local edition `store_memory` gets no owner because the caller context carries a `user_id` only from a Clerk id (consumers/chatbot/service.py:215-219; modules/tools/discovery/platform_executor.py:1282-1284), and a `scope: private` row with no owner is visible to nobody (injection_filter.py:61-76). userStories.title: One answer on the screen, never two and never none: the retraction names what was streamed, a blank retry never replaces an answer
userStories.description: Cause (G1, G2): `_note_round` retracts `streamed_rounds[-1].content` (consumers/chatbot/service.py:2054-2070) but that content can differ from what was streamed (think tags stripped in core/llm/reasoning.py:21-36; the owner-words rewrite runs per delta live and again on the whole text, core/llm/owner_words_stream.py:140-160; the apology stripped in nudges.py); the frontend deletes the last exact occurrence (frontend/lib/chat/narration.ts:17-21) and, when it does not match, leaves both (A108, A209, A622). The F205 retry and `kept_if_blank` (service.py:2151-2170; modules/tools/execution/nudges.py:216-230) can keep the original answer after its retraction was already sent, leaving the screen empty (eval M-terms-a turn 2).
acceptanceCriteria: The server records, per round, the exact text it streamed (the concatenated deltas after every live rewrite) and retracts THAT text, so `withoutNarration` always matches; a rewrite that happens after streaming never changes what is retracted. → DONE — faae24367: core/llm/screen_watch.py `watched` (a decorator on in_owner_words) joins the text deltas each streamed call delivered AFTER the live owner-words rewrite and reports them with the response to the turn's Screen (consumers/chatbot/on_screen.py, set by @keeps_one_answer_on_screen on _stream_response_with_agent_scoped); StreamingHandler.format_aisdk_narration now carries that round's streamed text (on_screen.narrated / retracted, looked up by the round's content), so the think block lifted out and the whole-text rewrite after the stream never change what is retracted; without a Screen the frame is as before.

A retraction is sent only when a non-blank replacement follows: `kept_if_blank`/the F205 retry decide first; when the original stands, no retraction frame is sent and the saved answer equals the screen. → DONE — faae24367: Screen.retraction holds a retraction (the frame is '' and @settles_held_retractions on _stream_tool_loop drops it) while the reply after the nudged round is blank; at the loop's final answer a held round is retracted only if the answer replaced it, and dropped when the original is the answer (kept_if_blank, the F205 re-prompt) — the saved answer then equals the screen; a retraction later sent for the same round clears its hold (never sent twice). Judgement call, the smaller change: the retraction still goes out when the replacement returns (after its text streamed), as before, with the exact text.

userStories.title: HIGH · FX-015: the owner's standing rule drops out once the workspace holds 500 store_memory rows, and a repeated rule never gets an owner
userStories.description: Cause: (a) the standing-rules read (modules/context/sections/memory.py:460-474 → durable_store.get_where_any, :356-363) scrolls every row of the workspace namespace whose metadata.source is platform_tool or type/category preference (every member's and every agent's store_memory), capped at STANDING_RULES_SCAN_LIMIT (500, config.py:1281) in Qdrant point order (random UUIDs), and filters by owner afterwards in Python (injection_filter.standing_rules). Each store_memory adds a candidate (night 12 attempted 251 in one night), so past 500 which rules are read is arbitrary: the owner's rule is missing from the next turn, the A591-596 failure the story fixes; the code only logs a warning. (b) DurableMemoryStore.add dedupes on (namespace, content_hash) and returns the existing id without touching its payload (durable_store.py:243-248): night 12's 'from November we post Tuesdays' is stored ownerless in c1, so the owner saying it again on night 13 dedupes onto that row, which has no owner and never becomes a standing rule; a second member stating the same text gets the first member's row.
acceptanceCriteria: The read filters on the viewer in the store: metadata.owner == the viewer's subject id is a `must` condition of the scroll (beside the namespace), so the scan holds only the viewer's candidates; the cap then only bounds one person's rules, newest first (sorted by created_at after the read, or Qdrant order_by where the collection has the payload index), and a reached cap still logs. → DONE — modules/context/sections/memory.py _stored_rule_rows(workspace_id, viewer_subject_id) passes where={STANDING_RULE_OWNER_KEY: viewer} (injection_filter.py, 'metadata.owner') to DurableMemoryStore.get_where_any, which adds it as an exact-match must beside the namespace (the should is unchanged); a turn with no viewer reads nothing; STANDING_RULES_SCAN_LIMIT now bounds one person's rows, sorted newest first by created_at after the read (injection_filter.standing_rules), and a reached cap still logs (now naming the viewer); ensure_collection adds a metadata.owner keyword payload index (created_at is a keyword index, so Qdrant order_by is not available: sorted after the read).

A store_memory whose content dedupes onto an existing row with no owner (or another owner) gives the row this writer's owner and source where it has none, or stores a row for this owner (the dedupe key includes metadata.owner); either way the owner's restated rule is their standing rule on the next turn. → DONE — the smaller of the two: the dedupe key of an owned write includes metadata.owner (DurableMemoryStore._find_by_hash(namespace, content_hash, owner=metadata.owner) adds the owner as a must), so the owner restating a rule stored ownerless (or stated by another member) stores a row of the writer's own with their owner and source and it is their standing rule next turn; the existing row is never rewritten (re-owning an ownerless workspace row would hide it from the others); an ownerless write dedupes as before; the same person restating still dedupes to one row. test_f103's _find_by_hash stub takes the owner keyword.

orchestrator/tests/test_prd256_fix_standing_rules.py: 600 other members' and agents' platform_tool rows plus the owner's rule → the rule is in the next turn's block; the owner restating a rule that exists ownerless → it is in the block; another member's identical text → in their block, not in the owner's. → DONE — orchestrator/tests/test_prd256_fix_standing_rules.py, over the real DurableMemoryStore and an in-memory Qdrant (_InMemoryQdrant: must/should filters, paged scroll, upsert): test_the_owners_rule_is_read_past_600_other_rows (300 other members' owned + 300 agents' ownerless platform_tool rows, the rule written after all 600, the scan cap 500), test_the_owner_restating_a_rule_stored_ownerless_makes_it_theirs, test_another_members_identical_rule_is_theirs_not_the_owners (in OTHER's block, not the owner's, then the owner's own row), test_the_same_person_restating_a_rule_still_dedupes; the FX-015 fake and the filter-shape test read the owner condition.

userStories.description: Cause: FX-014 runs handoffs._handed_over on every verdict (handoffs.py:617-628; the base did so only on DELEGATE), and addressed_agents.addressed_by_name (addressed_agents.py:148-155) reads only the verb, the name and the task after it: no negation, no question about a hand-off already made, and keeps_it_with_auto is not consulted on this path. 'Don't ask OPS to check anything', 'Never have WRITER touch the About page', 'I told you not to let OPS post', 'Did you ask OPS to check the stock?', 'Why didn't you get OPS to check?' and 'Should I ask OPS to check?' each become ASSIGN to OPS whatever the tiers said, and the ticket directive files and starts it: the owner's 'don't' starts the work. P256-FIX-RVW-12's participle rule is a fixed list plus '-ed', so 'Have sales risen this week?', 'Have sales hit target?', 'Have Support caught up?', 'Have sales come in?' (an agent called Sales or Support) are hand-offs too.
acceptanceCriteria: addressed_agents.addressed_by_name: a hand-off verb negated in its clause (don't, do not, never, not, no need to, stop), a question about a hand-off (the sentence ends in '?' and opens with did, didn't, why, should, could, has, have you/we/I, or a wh-word before the verb), and a message keeps_it_with_auto holds hand nothing over; a present-perfect question ('Have <name> <word> …?') hands nothing over unless 'to <verb>' follows the name. → DONE — addressed_agents._forbidden_or_asked (commit 4bba96225): a hand-off verb negated in its clause (don't, do not, never, not, no need to, stop; at most NEGATED_GAP=4 words before the verb, no clause break; 'don't forget/fail/hesitate to' still hands over), a question about one (the sentence ends in '?' and opens with did, didn't, why, should, has, have you/we/I, or a wh-word before the verb) and keeps_it_with_auto hand nothing over; a present perfect 'Have <name> <word> …?' hands nothing over unless 'to <verb>' follows. Judgement call, the smaller change: 'could' counts only as 'could I/we' — 'Could you get OPS to …?' is a request, like the golden's 'Can you get MARKET-MANAGER to …?'. A negation split off by commas ('Do not, ever, ask OPS') is not read: a comma ends the clause so 'Don't worry, ask OPS to …' still hands over

userStories.description: Cause: FX-006's criterion is that 'was/were <done-verb>' joins COMPLETED_ACTION and 'was approved' gets the line; P256-FIX-RVW-1, written to clear a red F186 test, removed the whole 'was/were' alternative (claims_backed.py:27-29, :64-73), so 'The card was approved.', 'The email was sent to Declan.' and 'The ticket was created.' with no call are no claim at all, and the FX-006 table now lists 'The card was approved.' as a non-claim. The F186 sentence ('Ticket #1110 was completed at 03:04') carries a time; a narrower exemption keeps both. Separately, send verbs in no family (replied, shared, invited, refunded, texted) are backed by any done write (claims_backed.py:180-212): a GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT, or a store_memory, backs 'I've replied to Declan.' — the A697/RVW-5 shape for the verb D7 lists ('reply').
acceptanceCriteria: COMPLETED_ACTION reads 'was/were <done-verb>' again; a simple-past passive with a past-time anchor in its sentence (at <HH:MM>, yesterday, this morning, last week/night, on <date>, ago, earlier) is history, not a claim, so F186's sentences stay non-claims and 'The card was approved.' with no call gets the line. → DONE — 77729af71: COMPLETED_ACTION reads 'was/were <done-verb>' again (claims_backed.py); _counts exempts a simple-past passive only when its sentence holds a past time (_HISTORY: at HH:MM or am/pm, this morning/afternoon/evening, last week/night, on <weekday/date/the 3rd/2026-10-03>, ago, earlier, yesterday; 'on 2 channels' is no date), so F186's 'Ticket #1110 was completed at 03:04' and 'Your two cards were approved this morning.' stay non-claims and 'The card was approved.' with no call gets the line. Smaller judgement call, so restoring the shape does not put a line over Auto's own refusal text (service.py's 'Nothing was done yet.', the tools' 'nothing was changed'): a was/were passive whose subject denies (nothing/none/no <noun>), a relative clause (that/which/who were …) and refused/denied/failed/skipped (added to _STATES) are no claim. A sweep of every string literal in orchestrator/tests and tests/sim through the old and new claims(): 0 claims lost, only was/were gains, none in an answer a test asserts clean.

FAMILIES: replied, texted and dm'd join the sent family; shared and invited need a write naming share/invite or a send; refunded needs refund or a payment write. → DONE — 77729af71: the sent family gains replied, texted, dm'd (and dmed; _DONE_VERB reads dm'd/dm’d, _verb now takes the matched verb whole); shared → a send or a write naming share/shares/sharing; invited → a send or a write naming invite/invites/invitation(s); refunded → a write naming refund(s) or payment(s) (a send does not back it).

userStories.title: MEDIUM · FX-017: a nudged draft is retracted twice when its retry only calls tools, and the second retraction takes the answer off the screen
userStories.description: Cause: service.py _note_round (:1865-1881) retracts streamed_rounds[-1] whenever the round before the current one ended with no tool call; a retry that calls tools with no text is never appended to streamed_rounds (:1878 needs content), so the nudged draft D stays streamed_rounds[-1]. Trace: D 'I've approved #0231.' streams, no call → nudged; the retry calls platform_update_task_status with no text → retraction of D (1st, correct; Screen.retraction returns D.said since the latest round is not blank); the tools run; the answer A 'I've approved #0231.' streams → _note_round(A) sees D as streamed_rounds[-1] again → Screen.retraction(D) finds D in the earlier rounds and A not blank → a 2nd frame with D's text. The frontend (narration.ts:18-21) deletes the last occurrence of D's text, which is now A: the screen shows no answer (or a mangled one when A only contains D, 'Done.' inside '…moved it to Done.'). FX-017's tests cover draft → text answer (:184) but not draft → tool-only retry → answer; Screen's 'never sent twice' covers only a held round.
acceptanceCriteria: A nudged round is retracted at most once per turn: Screen records the rounds it has retracted (sent or held-then-settled) and returns None for one already retracted, or _note_round stops treating a retracted round as the latest (whichever is smaller; no edit inside _stream_tool_loop's body beyond what the shape gate allows). → DONE — Screen keeps _gone, the rounds it retracted (a sent retraction, or a held one settled as replaced): retraction() returns None for a round already gone (also on the failover path, which now finds the round through _latest), settled() never repeats one; _note_round in service.py is untouched (the smaller change, inside on_screen.py)

test_prd256_fix_one_answer_on_screen.py: draft (no call) → nudge → a retry with tool calls and no text → the answer equal to the draft: exactly one retraction frame, and the frontend's rule (ported in the test) leaves the answer on the screen; the same with an answer that contains the draft ('Done.' / '…moved it to Done.'); the existing cases unchanged. → DONE — tests/test_prd256_fix_one_answer_on_screen.py: draft CLAIM (no call) → nudge → a retry with platform_update_task_status and no text → the answer equal to the draft: exactly one retraction, _screen_after (narration.ts withoutNarration, ported) leaves the answer; the same with 'Done.' → "I've moved #0231 to Done."; Screen unit tests: a tool-only retry then the same answer retracts once, a held round settled is never retracted again; the existing cases unchanged

userStories.title: MEDIUM · FX-006: stative and elliptical passives, first-person simple past and comma-listed claims escape the per-claim rule
userStories.description: Cause: COMPLETED_ACTION (claims_backed.py:69-80) reads 'I've <verb>', 'has/have been', 'was/were', 'is now <verb>' and a few fixed shapes; _AND_THEN (:106) reads a second verb only after 'and'/'then'. Probed with the module's own regexes (stub imports), each returns no claim: 'The task is done.', 'The post is published.', 'The post is scheduled for 5pm.', 'The ticket is created.', 'The post got sent.', 'It went out this morning.' (history, fine) vs 'It went out.', 'Email sent.', 'Posted!', 'I sent the email to Declan.', 'I created the task.', 'I emailed the supplier and created the ticket.'; and "I've created the ticket, emailed Sam." with only create_task done → no line for 'emailed'. With the families deleted (FX-007, D10) this rule is the only guard, and the hunt's 'a passive shape escapes' names exactly these.
acceptanceCriteria: COMPLETED_ACTION gains: 'is/are <done-participle>' (published, scheduled, created, sent, approved, done, closed, cancelled, …, not a _STATES word: 'is based', 'is called'), 'got/went/gone <participle|out|live>', a sentence that is only '<Noun> <participle>.' or '<Participle>!' ('Email sent.', 'Posted!'), and the first-person simple past 'I (just|also|…) <done-verb>' (not a _LOOKING verb); each under the existing plan-word, reply-content, history (_PAST/_HISTORY) and denial exemptions. → DONE — claims_backed.COMPLETED_ACTION gains the groups state ('is/are' or it's/that's/they're + an outcome participle: published, scheduled, created, sent, approved, done, closed, cancelled, completed, saved, booked, paid, …, 'set up'; a state such as 'is based', 'is called', 'is set to', 'is paused' is none), said ('got/went/gone <outcome|out|live>'; 'It went out.' is the send 'sent', 'went live' says only work happened), mine ('I (just|also|then|…) <family verb>', the families' verbs, so 'I wanted', 'I noticed' are none) and bare (a sentence that is only up to three words + a family verb + '.'/'!', no auxiliary and no negation: 'Email sent.', 'Posted!', not 'Rosa has ordered.', 'Not sent yet.', 'isn’t done'); each under the plan-word (now also 'as soon as'), reply-content, history (_PAST, and _HISTORY for the past shapes: 'It went out this morning.', 'I sent the invoice at 9am.') and denial/relative exemptions, plus a read's finding for the stative and 'went' shapes ('I found that the boxes are posted on Monday', F316's pinned answer); 'I made a mistake' is no work (_NO_WORK_AFTER). A stative with a time is NOT exempted as history ('is scheduled for 5pm on Monday' stays a claim): the judgement call, the smaller exemption

_AND_THEN also reads a participle after ',' or ';' that continues the claim's list ("I've created the ticket, emailed Sam." is created AND emailed), not one that starts a new clause with its own subject. → DONE — _AND_THEN's second branch reads a participle after ',' or ';' (optionally 'and/then/also'), not a _STATES word ("…, called 'Wholesale reply'" is none) and not a new clause with its own subject ('…, Sam emailed' is none): "I've created the ticket, emailed Sam." is created and emailed

userStories.title: MEDIUM · D7/FX-010/RVW-19: a brief Auto writes with a lead-in word or a common outbound verb keeps review_mode auto
userStories.description: Cause: brief_sends._verbs (brief_sends.py:60-66) reads a message verb only as a sentence's first word or after and/then, and MESSAGE_VERBS/SENDS_WORDS (:28-34) miss common outbound verbs. Each of these Auto-written briefs keeps review_mode auto: 'Please email the supplier to confirm delivery', 'Also post the menu on Instagram', 'Just message Declan the times', 'Contact the supplier to confirm the order', 'Reach out to Declan', 'Let Declan know the box is late', 'Get back to the customer', 'Respond to the review', 'Notify the team', 'Invite Sam to the call', 'Submit the form'. D7: 'Auto-created briefs that send/order/publish default to review_mode human'. The Composio card still asks at the send (FX-011), so what is lost is the ticket's review before it closes.
acceptanceCriteria: _verbs skips leading politeness and adverbs before taking a sentence's verb ('please', 'also', 'just', 'now', 'kindly', 'then', 'first', 'remember to', 'make sure to', 'can you', 'could you'), and reads the word after 'to' in 'ask/get/have <someone> to <verb>'. → DONE — brief_sends._verbs is replaced by _clauses + _without_lead_in + _messages (118ae9628): each sentence is split at and/then into clauses, each clause read from its verb past LEAD_INS (please, also, just, now, kindly, then, first) and LEAD_IN_PHRASES (remember to, make sure to, can you, could you), repeatedly ('Could you please text Sam'); after ASKS (ask/get/have) the verb after 'to' is read the same way, recursively ('Get the team to reach out to Kerbside')

The outbound verbs join the brief's lists: contact, notify, respond, invite, submit, share (as a verb), 'reach out', 'let <x> know', 'get back to'; 'Draft a reply to Declan', 'Draft the email', 'Prepare a post for review' and 'Read the supplier's email' keep auto. → DONE — MESSAGE_VERBS gains contact, notify, respond, invite, submit, share (verb position only, so 'Update the contact list', 'Draft the invite' and 'Draft a response' keep auto); OUTBOUND_PHRASES ('reach out', 'get back to') and TELL_PHRASES ('let <x> know', anywhere in the clause) count; 'Draft a reply to Declan', 'Draft the email', 'Prepare a post for review' and 'Read the supplier's email' keep auto

userStories.description: Cause: addressed_agents._forbidden_or_asked (addressed_agents.py:185) treats every sentence-initial 'Have <name> …?' with no 'to <verb>' after the name as a present-perfect question, but _task_follows/_bare_verb already exclude a participle or an auxiliary after the name, so the rule only ever fires on a bare verb: 'Have OPS check the stock?', 'Have WRITER draft the About page?', 'Have RESEARCHER find the Leith cafés?' go back to the tiers. userStories.title: MEDIUM · FX-006/RVW-25: common claim shapes still escape — 'reviewed and approved', bullets and ✅ lists, subject-less verbs, 'Done —', 'went ahead and', 'been successfully', "'s been"
userStories.description:
Cause (each returns claims == [] with no writes, probed at HEAD): (a) a looking verb before the done verb hides the claim — "I've reviewed and approved the card.", "I've checked the board and approved #0931.", "I've confirmed and sent the email." (the I've-shape fails its _LOOKING lookahead and _coordinated extends only from an accepted match; approvals are what PRD-256 gates); (b) list shapes — '- Task created
- Email sent', '✅ Task created
✅ Email sent to Sam', 'Done:
- Task created'; 'Done — email's out to Declan and the ticket's closed.' (^done only before . ! ,); (c) subject-less verb + object — 'Sent the email to Declan.', 'Cancelled the order for you.', 'Card #0931 moved to Done.'; (d) 'I went ahead and cancelled the order.' ('gone ahead and' is listed, 'went ahead and' is not); (e) 'Task #0931 has been successfully created.' (adverb after been), "The card's been approved." (noun + 's been).
acceptanceCriteria: Each shape above is read as a claim: 'I've/I <looking verb> … and|then <done verb>' claims the done verb; a line or sentence that opens (after a bullet, ✅, 'Okay,', 'Just') with a done-verb past form is a claim; 'Done' followed by ':' or a dash is the bare done claim; 'went ahead and' joins _FIRST_ADVERBS; adverbs after 'been'; "<noun>'s been <verb>" is the has-been shape. Quoted lines, fenced blocks, plan words and history keep their exemptions. → DONE — f0ecf471a consumers/chatbot/claims_backed.py: _LOOKED_AND (I've/I <looking verb> … and|then <family verb>), the opens group (_LEAD bullet/tick/'Okay,' + _FIRST_ADVERBS 'Just', a family verb with an object after it, _OBJECT; or _NUMBERED 'Card 0931 moved'), the bare group takes a '-' bullet with no full stop, the ticked group (✅ + ≤3 words + family verb), 'done' + ':' or a dash, 'went ahead and' in _FIRST_ADVERBS, _ADVERBS after 'been', <noun>'s been (never nothing's/who's/there's); 'Done —' before a claim of its sentence introduces it (_DONE_FIRST). Quotes, fences, plan words, history, questions keep their exemptions. Judgement (smaller change): a looking-then-done claim and a verb-first line read only a family verb (+ made), so 'I've checked and decided to wait' is no claim; an agent's run still reads only its first person. A sweep of every test string literal (orchestrator/tests, tests/sim) before/after: 42 new claims, none in an answer a test asserts clean; one changed ("Done, it's approved." drops its bare done, its backing unchanged)

userStories.title: MEDIUM · FX-006: a read-only platform call counts as a done write, and a verb in no family is backed by any write
userStories.description: Cause: turn_account.is_read (turn_account.py:65-72, _READS) misses read tools whose registry permission_level is 'read' — platform_load_skill, platform_fleet_status, platform_harness_status, platform_graph_*, platform_codegraph_* — so load_skill alone is a DONE write receipt ('Skill done') and backs 'Done.', 'Your post is now live on LinkedIn.' and every no-family verb. And unbacked_claims (claims_backed.py:409) lets ANY done write back a verb in no family: platform_store_memory + "I've rejected the card." / "I've stopped the mission." / "I've revoked the key." / "I've reassigned the card to OPS." → no line (probed), which is FX-006's 'silenced by another successful write' failure for those verbs.
acceptanceCriteria: A receipt's kind (read/write) comes from the action registry's permission_level where the action is registered (the stem list stays for Composio slugs and unregistered names); a no-family verb needs a done write whose name shares its stem (reject_, stop_, restart_, revoke_, reassign_/assign_, charge_/pay, escalat…) — else the line; 'Done.', 'is now live', 'you should now see' still accept any done write. → DONE — 615eea4c0 modules/tools/execution/turn_account.py is_read: a registered action's permission_level first (_registered_level, the registry's get), the _READS stems only for unregistered names; Composio slugs keep their whole-word read list. platform_load_skill, platform_fleet_status, platform_harness_status, platform_graph_*, platform_codegraph_* are read receipts; platform_checkpoint_thread and workspace_get_public_url (registered write) are now writes. consumers/chatbot/claims_backed.py: a verb in no family takes _unfamiliar — a done write a word of whose name starts with the verb's stem (_verb_stems: rejected→reject, stopped→stop, revoked→revok, escalated→escalat) or one of the words its write goes by (_GOES_BY: reassign→assign, charg→pay, turn→reject/decline, put→create/add/assign/move/update, mark→approve/update/move, draft→create/generate/write/save, fil→create, kept→memory/store/save); 'Done.', 'is now live', 'you should now see' (SAYS_DONE) and 'I've made the changes' take any done write; not_done_line names an unbacked no-family verb when another write went through ('I haven't rejected anything in this reply'), and the nudge still reads only known families (RVW-7). Judgement (smaller change): _GOES_BY holds only the no-family verbs the existing tests back by another write's name (f261 'marked it as done', 'put it on your board', f379 'drafted' a post, F381 'filed a task', F324 'kept this in my own memory'); platform_field_inject has no explicit permission_level, so the registry's default reads it as a read (its level is a guardrail input to the policy plane, left as it is)

userStories.title: MEDIUM · FX-007: four bugs the families fixed are now asserted as cleared — F308 steps said to pause, F261-A a reply ending on a promise, F351 a letter backed by a ticket, F324 'all agents know'
userStories.description: Cause: FX-007's notes take 'Promises, checks, counts and figures are cleared' as a judgement call, and the base's tests were inverted, not replaced: test_prd256_families_deleted.py rows 'F308 steps said to pause' ('Each step will pause for your approval.' over a mission with checks_each_step False → None), 'F261 a promise to send' ('I will now send this updated brief to the agent.', night 8 #0181, nothing sent → None; test_f261_a…:32 now asserts no nudge), 'F324 stored for the team' ("I've stored it in my memory so that all agents know." → backed), and 'saved' backed by any create_ ("I've created the letter to Maya and saved it to your Deliverables." over create_task alone → backed; F351 required a document write). Each is a wrong statement the owner acts on (a step they think waits for them; a send they think is under way; a document that does not exist). PRD-256 W2 US-012's AC: none weakened without a replacement test covering the same sentence; CLAUDE.md §12: descoping is the owner's call.
acceptanceCriteria: Through the receipts rule (no family module comes back): a claim that each step pauses needs a receipt with checks_each_step true; created/saved with a document noun (letter, document, PDF, docx, report) needs a document-making write (generate_document, create_document, upload_); a claim that the team or agents know needs a write other than memory; a reply whose last sentence announces work now ('I will now <family verb>…') with no call of that family gets the F108 announced-step nudge. Gerard may instead confirm clearing any of the four: record his decision in this story's notes and leave that row as it is. → DONE — 3a2b46716 new consumers/chatbot/claims_by_kind.py (174 lines), read by claims_backed (no family module back): document_backs — created/generated/saved whose object or passive subject is a letter, document, PDF, docx or report (saved: or to Deliverables; the noun the head of its phrase, never 'the report task', 'report preferences', 'an agent called REPORT GENERATOR') needs a write that makes a document (DOCUMENT_MAKES, create_document, upload_document/upload_, submit_report, or a writing verb on a document word: NOTION_CREATE_PAGE, GOOGLEDRIVE_UPLOAD_FILE, platform_update_document); 'each step will pause/wait/stop' needs a done write whose receipt effect is 'each step waits for your OK' (EACH_STEP_WAITS, now the one string receipts._SAID uses); 'all agents are aware' / 'so that all agents know' / 'the team has been told' / 'everyone now knows' needs a done write other than memory; a reply whose last sentence is 'I will now <verb> …' with a family verb and no done write of that family is unbacked — receipts.unbacked_promise feeds nudges.announced_step(text, outcomes) so the tool loop sends ANNOUNCED_STEP_MSG (tool_loop line replaced in place, 816 lines). The not-done line says the steps and the team in their own words (claims_backed._not_said). userStories.title: MEDIUM · FX-017: a blank F205 retry after an apology-stripped answer leaves the screen empty
userStories.description: Cause: on_screen.Screen.settled (on_screen.py:89-95) decides a held round was replaced by string equality (r.content != content). nudges.kept_if_blank → without_the_apology (nudges.py:202-245) returns a dataclasses.replace copy with the opening apology removed; the Screen recorded the original. Trace: a write is refused; draft D claims work and is nudged; retry R streams 'You're right, my apologies. platform_update_agent was refused…' (D retracted, correct); the loop's answer is R′ (no apology); F205 (_owner_words) re-prompts on the internal name and the re-prompt comes back blank; _note_round(blank) holds R's retraction; settled(R′) sees R.content ≠ R′.content and retracts R; R′ carries streamed=True (the copy keeps it), so no tail is emitted. acceptanceCriteria: Screen settles by where the answer came from: a held round stands when the answer is its response object or a copy of it (the answer is streamed and its whitespace-normalised text is a suffix of the round's); otherwise it is retracted. → DONE — on_screen._stands: a held round stands when the answer is its response (Round.response) or a streamed copy whose whitespace-normalised words end the round's at a sentence boundary; Screen.settled uses it instead of equal text. userStories.title: HIGH · F397/F400: a service's model and its provider come from different vendors once the System LLM is Anthropic
userStories.description: Cause (TESTER, 9 Oct, after system_llm → anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5): memory_integration takes its provider from system_llm (core/llm/manager.py:49 maps it) but its model from config.MEMORY_DISTILL_MODEL, which falls back to DEFAULT_LLM_MODEL 'google/gemini-2.5-flash' (config.py:331-346, core/llm/defaults.py:14) when memory.distill_model is unset → the Anthropic client is sent model 'google/gemini-2.5-flash' and 404s on every turn's fact distill and thread checkpoint (smart_memory.py:658, modules/memory/thread_checkpoint.py:294). Same shape: the cross-model verifier (modules/coordination/run_verdict.py:275-290, services/watch_decider.py:145-158) maps an Anthropic executor to 'openai/gpt-4o-mini' (config.py:1059-1083 defaults) and builds it on the system_llm provider → 404, finished agent runs go unjudged. Unblocked locally only by settings rows (memory.distill_model, coordination.verifier_model_mapping, coordination.verifier_fallback_model).
acceptanceCriteria: A model id passed to create_llm_manager with a service whose provider comes from a settings category is checked against that provider before the client is built: a vendor-prefixed id ('google/…', 'openai/…') on a non-OpenRouter provider, or a bare Claude id on a non-Anthropic provider, is resolved to the provider that serves it when that provider has a key, otherwise the call falls back to the category's own model with one warning naming service, model and provider (never a 404 per turn). → DONE — core/llm/vendor_fit.fitted, called by create_llm_manager when a model comes without a provider: get_provider_and_model_from_settings gives the category's provider; a 'vendor/…' id on a provider without hosts_vendor_models (azure, bedrock, huggingface keep their own ids) or a bare id providers.mismatched_vendor reads as another vendor's ('claude-…' on openrouter) is routed to the first provider with a key in the manager's own chain (credential store, operator workspace key, env): the id without its prefix when the prefix is the provider's own, OpenRouter as written, the vendor's direct API (bare ids: the vendor, then OpenRouter with its prefix); none → the category's model, one lru_cache'd warning naming service, model and provider (67a1f4655)

MEMORY_DISTILL_MODEL with no memory.distill_model setting resolves to the system_llm category's model (not the hard-coded Gemini id); the verifier's default mapping, when the system_llm provider is anthropic, picks a Claude model different from the executor's (e.g. claude-sonnet-5-5 for a Fable/Opus executor, claude-haiku-5-5 for a Sonnet one) instead of openai/gpt-4o-mini. → DONE — config.MEMORY_DISTILL_MODEL: memory.distill_model → env → system_llm.model → DEFAULT_LLM_MODEL; COORDINATOR_VERIFIER_MODEL_MAPPING / _FALLBACK_MODEL default through vendor_fit.default_verifier_mapping/_fallback: an anthropic system_llm gives 'sonnet=claude-haiku-5-5,anthropic=claude-sonnet-5-5' and claude-sonnet-5-5 (core/llm/defaults.py), others the old strings; verification._select_verifier_model tries a non-family (tier) key before the family, so Opus/Fable/Haiku → claude-sonnet-5-5, Sonnet → claude-haiku-5-5 (67a1f4655)

userStories.title: HIGH · Gerard 11 Oct: sending a card back to its agent waits for the owner's click
userStories.description: Decision (Gerard, 11 Oct, after the four-model benchmark): a send-back — a card the agent has worked on (status review or done) moved back to assigned / in_progress / inbox for rework, from chat ('turn it down', 'redo it', 'send #1219 back') — is owner-only, like approve and cancel. Today owner_only.is_owner_only (modules/tools/discovery/owner_only.py:118-134) makes a CARD_MOVES call owner-only only when closing_status() (:170-176) reads done/cancelled/closed, so platform_update_task_status {status: 'assigned'} on a Review card runs at once (eval N5-a on Haiku 5.5: 'I've sent #1219 back … It's now in Assigned', no card). Giving a NEW inbox card to an agent (inbox → assigned, the hand-off lane) stays free.
acceptanceCriteria: is_owner_only reads a card move as owner-only when it closes the card (as today) OR when it sends back a worked card: the card's current status is review or done (read from the board, workspace-scoped) and the new status is one of assigned, in_progress, inbox. The rule lives beside closing_status (one helper, e.g. sends_back(card_status, new_status)), not a second list. → DONE — owner_only.sends_back(card_status, new_status) beside closing_status (WORKED_STATUSES review/done × REWORK_STATUSES assigned/in_progress/inbox, one helper, no second list); is_owner_only reads a CARD_MOVES call as owner-only when closing_status OR send_backs.sends_back_a_card: each card named (task_id, task_ids, by number via ticket_id_named) read from BoardTask filtered by workspace_id; send_back:true reads as Assigned; the executor wrapper (self.db), the confirmation gate (call.db) and follows_the_owner._rules_for (db) pass the board, so a send-back gets CARD_RULES (D1: the card before the signature rule); without a board (db None) a move is judged by its status alone. Judgement calls (the smaller change, OWNER to decide): a Re-brief (platform_update_task with a new description, FX-013 drops its status) is NOT read as a send-back; a card in blocked/failed/in_progress is not 'worked' (AC: review or done), so Review → Blocked → Assigned is two free moves; a mission's own card is excluded (the board's send_back refuses it) (bcddaf606)

userStories.title: HIGH · F416: a dead backend is never restarted
userStories.description: Night 14 (12–13 Oct, main df3e213eb, Auto on Haiku 5.5: 561 asks, 74% first time, receipts match 69%; ~/.automatos-sim/customer-night/2026-10-12-night14 MORNING-REPORT.md / DIARY.md; ledger F416): after the OOM kill the container stayed 'running' and unhealthy with nothing serving for ~5 h (docker-compose.yml backend: restart: unless-stopped, which docker does not apply to an unhealthy container).
acceptanceCriteria: The backend's process exits when it can no longer serve (the uvicorn master exits when its worker is killed, or the healthcheck's failure ends the container's main process), so restart: unless-stopped brings it back; the healthcheck interval/retries mean a dead backend is restarted within ~2 minutes. No new container or dependency (no autoheal image). → DONE — new orchestrator/docker-healthcheck.sh is the one probe (curl -fsS /health on ${PORT:-8000}, --max-time AUTOMATOS_HEALTHCHECK_TIMEOUT 10); Docker's healthcheck (both Dockerfile stages, compose backend) and the entrypoint run it. docker-entrypoint.sh: with AUTOMATOS_LIVENESS_WATCHDOG=true (envs/api.defaults; off in the image, so Railway still exec's its CMD) run_supervised runs the command as its child and watch_liveness probes every 30 s; armed at the first passing probe (a slow boot is start_period's, F228), 3 failures in a row log 'The backend stopped serving', TERM then KILL after 10 s, and the entrypoint exits 1, so the container exits and restart: unless-stopped restarts it: worst case 3 × (30 + 10) + 10 = 130 s; a server that exits passes its status on; TERM/INT are forwarded (docker stop). Dev CMD is now `&& exec uvicorn` so the signals reach uvicorn, not dash. No new container, image or dependency (uvicorn 0.24's --reload and --workers supervisors never restart a dead worker, hence the entrypoint) (6ecbf90c7)

docs or a test pins it: a test of the entrypoint/healthcheck script (e.g. scripts/docker/backend-healthcheck) that a failed check exits non-zero and the entrypoint propagates a dead worker as the container's exit. → DONE — orchestrator/tests/test_prd256_fix_dead_backend_restarts.py runs the real entrypoint under bash with a stub server and probe at 1 s: a server that served then stops answering is TERMed after 2/2 failures and the entrypoint exits non-zero with the server gone; a hung server that ignores TERM is KILLed after the grace; a server that exits 3 gives 3; a never-serving slow boot is never stopped; a healthy one is left alone; TERM to the entrypoint reaches the server; without the flag no probe runs. The real healthcheck against a local HTTP server: 200 passes, 500/503 and nothing listening exit non-zero. Wiring: compose runs the probe, mounts it, restart unless-stopped, api.defaults turns the watchdog on, the watchdog's defaults equal compose's interval/retries and restart within 150 s, both image stages copy it, dev CMD exec's uvicorn. docker-healthcheck.sh added to the two LF line-ending pins (6ecbf90c7). 'Only reads' fails closed and needs both witnesses: every stored capability in READ_CAPABILITIES, and the slug's verb (the word after the app, GMAIL_FETCH_…) a read word (send_words.READ_WORDS) with no send/order/payment word (LEAVES_THE_WORKSPACE) or write word anywhere in it, so GMAIL_SEND_DRAFT stored as data.query, SHOPIFY_LIST_ORDERS, GMAIL_GET_OR_CREATE_LABEL or an unknown verb still meet the match. userStories.title: CRITICAL · F444: two owner clicks accepted, then silently dropped — cards raised for calls their handler refuses
userStories.description: Night 17 (15–16 Oct, main 5b586cbaa, Auto on Haiku 5.5: 455 asks, 77.7% first time, receipts 97.7%; ~/.automatos-sim/customer-night/2026-10-16-night17 MORNING-REPORT.md / DIARY.md / chats.jsonl / answers.jsonl / logs; ledger F444): two clicks returned 200 and did nothing; both found only because the owner asked afterwards. (1) Mission: chats.jsonl L373 (23:44:02Z, chat cd451f3c) platform_create_mission with Auto's 115-word goal → 'waiting · card raised: start a mission' (#2816), granted 23:44:59Z; on the click the handler refused NOT_THEIR_GOAL (owner's words 6/115 = 0.052 < OWNERS_GOAL 0.3), the grant was given back, and the owner learned it only at L378 ('The system refused the mission because the goal wasn't in your words'). (2) #1767 (task 3058) was filed at L442 by platform_create_task with approval_action create_blog and no agent, so it was born in Review (handlers_board_tasks.initial_board_status 77-91); 'turn #1767 down' (L450, 00:21:59Z, chat c22d682b) → platform_update_task_status {status:'assigned', note} → card #2827 'send … back to its agent', granted 00:23:02Z (the ledger's '01:52' is a diary label); on the click api/board_tasks.send_back raised 422 'Cannot reject a task with no assigned agent' and the card never moved (iter7.log L389: review, times_sent_back 0). L468's retry ('Send #1767 back to WRITER then…', no agent in the call) raised #2832 on the same path (granted 08:56:48Z, not re-read). Even a working send-back was wrong there: approving #1767 runs a fixed create_blog topic (board_tasks.py 678-693) that no redo can change. Cause, verified by TESTER on origin/main 0d9f0ac59 (no commit since 14 Oct touches these files): owner-only cards are raised by owner_only._on_the_click → platform_ask (253-258, 420-452) with no check that the handler would accept the call. The mission word rule (mission_create_checks.refusal_for_mission 31, 43-52, 88-91, run by mission_asks.asks_as_the_owner_says 61-74) runs only on the click, and platform_create_mission has requires_confirmation=False (actions_mission_create.py:105), so _on_the_click is its only ask. The Reject's preconditions (api/board_tasks.send_back 884-899: SENDABLE_BACK 422, redo_refusal 409, no agent 422 at 898-899) are never checked before the card; send_back_act (send_backs.py 104-110) falls back to 'its agent'. Silence: _resume_tool_call writes executed_result {success:false} and the /grant route still returns 200 (api/approval_grants.py 170-205); frontend GrantCard.act (components/command-center/governance/approvals-inbox.tsx 68-78, reused by ticket-approvals.tsx 18, 55) always toasts success; click_results.said_in_the_chat (78-92) posts the failure only into the asking chat (c22d682b was never reopened); tests/sim/customer.py cmd_grant (106-111) discards the response. Latent defect found on the way: platform_update_task {agent, status:'assigned', note} on an answered card goes through agent_refs.gives_the_card_on_update (167-185) → an_answered_card_runs_again (GIVEN_TO_YOU) and never reaches send_back (keeps_the_board_rules sees status == new_status, ticket_moves.py 105-106): sent_back unset, times_sent_back 0, and the owner's note never reaches the redo (redo_block reads review_feedback/owner_corrections only, services/ticket_redo.py 206-243, 424-427); test_prd256_fix_send_back_waits_for_the_click.py:131-145 asserts only the ask's wording. To confirm (TESTER, read-only DB): SELECT id, granted_by, details->'executed_result' FROM approval_grants WHERE id IN (2816, 2827, 2832).
acceptanceCriteria: Missions refused before the card: owner_only._on_the_click (253-258), when grant is None and action == 'platform_create_mission', computes mission_create_checks.refusal_for_mission(db, ws, params, mission_owner_words.owners_words(db, ws, params)) on the injected `params` (only those carry _origin_chat_id, platform_executor.py:1186-1190, 1262), not `asked`; a refusal returns {success: False, error: refusal} and creates no grant; otherwise platform_ask as now. → DONE — fdc15f649: mission_create_checks.refused_before_the_mission_card (refusal_for_mission on owners_words of the handler's injected params) runs in owner_only._on_the_click when no grant is found, before platform_ask; a refusal returns {success: False, error} and no grant.

The click judges a mission by the copy rule only: mission_asks.asks_as_the_owner_says (64-74), when params carry owner_only.CLICKED_BY, calls refusal_for_mission(..., clicked=True), which runs only _already_waiting (the word rules already ran before the card). CLICKED_BY exists only when granted_by starts with 'user:' (owner_only.py:259-260, 528-533); the /grant route always records actor_ref(ctx) (approval_grants.py:75-80). → DONE — fdc15f649: refusal_for_mission(..., clicked=True) runs only _already_waiting; mission_asks.asks_as_the_owner_says passes clicked=bool(params[CLICKED_BY]).

One Reject rule: new services/send_back_rules.py with a pure send_back_refusal(db, task) -> Optional[(int, str)] holding api/board_tasks.send_back 890-899 verbatim ((422, 'Only a ticket in review or done can be sent back (currently: …)'), (409, redo_refusal text), (422, 'Cannot reject a task with no assigned agent')); send_back raises HTTPException(code, detail) from it, so codes and texts are unchanged for /reject, ticket_moves._send_back and every pinned test. → DONE — fdc15f649: services/send_back_rules.send_back_refusal holds the three checks (SENDABLE_BACK moved there); api/board_tasks.send_back raises HTTPException(code, detail) from it, codes and texts unchanged.

Send-backs refused before the card: new modules/tools/discovery/send_back_checks.py sendable_back(db, ws, action, params) -> (params, refused, left_out), called in owner_only.platform_ask after bound_to_the_agent / bound_to_the_subject / bound_to_the_playbook (435-440), in the same `if not refused` chain as refused_before_the_card and rebrief_that_closes (441-442), so it covers both _on_the_click (258) and the confirmation gate (confirmation_gate.py:89-91). Scope is exactly what ticket_moves hands to send_back: cards in send_backs._sent_back for which ticket_moves._sends_it_back (exported under a public name) is True (answered → 'assigned', the send_back flag, or → 'in_progress' with a note, ticket_moves.py:117-122); review/done → inbox and → in_progress with no note are untouched. Per card: (ii) planning_data.approval_action set or approval_cards.is_an_approval_card(planning_data) → refused whatever agent is named: "{label} ('{title}') is a card for the owner's approval: approving it {does, e.g. starts a blog mission on '<topic>'}, and an agent's redo can't change that. Nothing was asked or done. To turn it down: platform_update_task_status {task_id: \"{number}\", status: \"cancelled\"} (waits for the owner's click). For a different topic, file a new card with that topic." — never offering a redo; otherwise send_back_refusal on board_drag_rules.as_patched(card, assigned_agent_id=<bound agent_id>) when platform_update_task carries an agent after binding, else on the card; the refusal names the card plus the Reject's detail, and for the no-agent 422 only adds 'Name the agent it goes to: platform_update_task {task_id, status: "assigned", agent_id, note: the owner's words}, or turn it down with status "cancelled" (each waits for the owner's click)' (ships only with the next AC). Bulk task_ids: drop only the failing cards from task_ids, return left_out = [(number, why)], appended to the ask's message ('Left off this card: #N, why') and an ask field left_out; nothing sendable left → the whole call refused naming each card; a single task_id that fails is refused whole. → DONE — fdc15f649: send_back_checks.sendable_back (board_sends_back = send_backs.cards_sent_back filtered by ticket_moves.sends_it_back, now public) runs in owner_only.platform_ask through _bound_and_checked after the bound_to_* chain, refused_before_the_card and rebrief_that_closes, so _on_the_click and the confirmation gate both read it. Approval cards refused naming the cancel (in Review) or a new card (Done, no cancel offered); other cards through send_back_refusal on as_patched(card, assigned_agent_id) for the edit tool, the no-agent 422 adding how to name the agent. Bulk: failing cards left off (left_out + 'Left off this card: #N, which …'); the call's own task_id failing, or every send-back failing, refuses the whole call (saying the call's other cards were not moved). On this branch a Re-brief is in that scope (N17-1's moved_to), so it is read the same way.

An agent-given send-back keeps the note: agent_refs.gives_the_card_on_update (172-184), when the same call sends an answered card back by the rule above, gives the card with the plain handlers_board_tasks.assign_board_task (484-536: sets assigned_agent_id, leaves the card where it is, no dispatch) instead of handlers_board_task_assign.assign_board_task; the existing update leg then reaches api.board_tasks.send_back (keep_previous_run(why=SENT_BACK), with_correction(note), review_feedback=note, SENT_BACK_SAID True), and _both (193-199) carries sent_back. A give without a send-back (platform_assign_task, an agent only, or status done) keeps an_answered_card_runs_again (test_f309_b, RVW-17). → DONE — fdc15f649: agent_refs._the_give: when board_sends_back holds the edit, the plain handlers_board_tasks.assign_board_task gives the card and the update leg reaches api send_back (note, owner_corrections, previous_runs 'sent back', sent_back carried by _both); else an_answered_card_runs_again as before (status done, agent only, platform_assign_task). A Re-brief naming another agent is now a real Re-brief with that agent (N17-1's flagged plain edit).

The click's surface is honest: executedOutcomeLine moves to frontend/lib/grant-outcome.ts and is re-exported from components/widgets/ToolApprovalWidget/index.tsx; GrantCard.act's Grant branch (approvals-inbox.tsx 68-78) reads res.grant.details.executed_result and calls toast.error(executedOutcomeLine(…)) when success === false, else toast.success — covering the ticket card (ticket-approvals.tsx:55) and the Governance inbox. Harness (test-only): tests/sim/customer.py cmd_grant (106-111) prints executed_result.success and error from the /grant response and writes them into answers.jsonl. → DONE — fdc15f649: frontend/lib/grant-outcome.ts holds executedOutcomeLine and executedResultOf, re-exported from ToolApprovalWidget; GrantCard.act toasts toast.error(executedOutcomeLine) when a Grant's executed_result.success === false (Governance inbox and the ticket card); tests/sim/customer.py cmd_grant prints and writes executed_success/executed_error into answers.jsonl (customer_ops.grant_outcome).

Gerard's calls, flagged (not deferred): (a) refusing chat send-backs of approval cards also blocks publish_blog approval cards that have an agent (handlers_blog.py:241) — confirm wanted; (b) on an approval card 'turn it down' routes to cancel plus a new card — confirm cancel (not a recorded decline) is the meaning; (c) same bug class, fold in here or file separately: review → in_progress with no note on a no-agent card raises a card the click refuses NO_AGENT_NO_PROGRESS (handlers_board_tasks.py:720-721); platform_update_task {send_back: true} with no note or description raises a card the click refuses NEEDS_THE_WORDS (ticket_edits.py:135-136); a bulk move over MAX_BULK_TASK_IDS raises a card the handler refuses whole (ticket_moves.py:60-61); gives with no status on an approval-action card never reach platform_ask. If folded in, each gets the same pre-card refusal and a test. → DONE — fdc15f649: flagged for Gerard. (a) built as written: a publish_blog approval card with an agent is refused too, and a Done approval card is refused with no cancel offered. (b) built as written: 'turn it down' on an approval card names platform_update_task_status {status: cancelled} (cancel, not a recorded decline). Same class, now covered: a Re-brief's no-agent refusal (its card was added by N17-1).
