userStories.title: HIGH · F445: 'did that go through?' reads the card's status, not its send-back, and offers to send it back again
userStories.description: Night 17 (15–16 Oct, main 5b586cbaa, Auto on Haiku 5.5: 455 asks, 77.7% first time, receipts 97.7%; ~/.automatos-sim/customer-night/2026-10-16-night17 MORNING-REPORT.md / DIARY.md / chats.jsonl / answers.jsonl / logs/iter4.log; ledger F445). chats.jsonl row 263 (1-indexed, chat cc4e3e29, turn ending 20:39:37Z): 'Send #1745 back…' → platform_update_task_status {task_id '#1745', status 'assigned', note} → waiting, 'the card waits for you to click it'; answers.jsonl:18 grant 2801 approved 20:40:48Z; probe iter4.log:172 card 3033 = #1745 'in_progress | sent_back 1' (~20:40:58Z), :214 '3033 review sent_back 1 updated 2026-10-15T20:43:03'. Row 268 'Did that one go through?' (turn 20:41:57.8–20:43:22.3Z; six asks fired together; ts is the end of the turn, tests/sim/customer.py:64-68) called only search_knowledge (automatic) and platform_get_task {'#1745'} and replied 'No, it hasn't gone through. #1745 still shows as in Review, with RESEARCHER's last result on it and no send-back… The card is still waiting on your click. Do you want me to send it back now…' — inviting a duplicate send-back. The send-back itself worked end to end. Cause, verified by TESTER on origin/main 0d9f0ac59 (git diff d7affad60..origin/main over discovery/, services/, consumers/chatbot/, formatting/ and api/board_tasks.py is empty): platform_get_task (platform_executor.py:1406) → handlers_board_tasks.get_board_task (435-481) returns id, title, description, raw_prompt, status, priority, review_mode, assigned_agent, tags, result[:2000], error_message and timestamps — nothing about a send-back. The send-back lives only in planning_data (api/board_tasks.send_back 884-919: keep_previous_run(why=SENT_BACK) :905, with_correction :907); services/ticket_redo.times_sent_back (173-180) is read only by board_task_view.py:27 (the HTTP board); _back_to_its_agent (944-955) blanks started_at, completed_at and result, so once the redo returns a sent-back card reads like one never sent back. Nothing the model reads gives the approval card's decision either: approval_grants is read only by platform_my_actions {ticket} (my_actions_clicks.decision_of 71-82, click_memory.numbers_of_the_card 114-122), routed for 'what did I decide', not called on row 268; card_numbers is not stored on the grant (tool_grants._grant_details 210-231). And the claim check would cut the right answer: 'It was sent back to RESEARCHER with your note.' matches the past shape (claims_backed.py:116) and "It's been sent back" the 's-been shape (114-115); neither is exempt (_history_or_denial 445-455 needs a time, _found_by_a_read 458-465 a read number, looked_up covers state only), so unbacked_where (582-603) returns them and the not-done line replaces the answer. Row 268's tool JSON is not in the night data (args only); read-after-20:43:03 is inferred from the wording, and either ordering yields a read with no send-back record. Open for Gerard: show the record on any person-driven turn or Auto's only; include mission-tool send-backs (platform_reject_mission) in the scan; workspace time zone for times.
acceptanceCriteria: Only on a person's own chat turn: 'platform_get_task' is added to platform_executor._DRIVER_AWARE_ACTIONS (355-360), so the strip-then-inject (1159-1167) always removes a model-supplied _driving_user_id and injects the server's (core/security/driving_user.py:33-37). get_board_task adds one call after the widget return (451-452) and the dict (461-481) — the file is already 844 lines: `if params.get('_driving_user_id'): answer['task'] = {**answer['task'], **ticket_redo.send_back_seen(db, workspace_id, task, params['_driving_user_id'])}`. Agent runs, CLI sessions (services/session_tools.py:774, 781-788), mission_refs._the_card (208-216, fresh params) and widget turns (VISITOR_TASK) get nothing.

The record, in services/ticket_redo.py (462 → ~580 lines): constants SENT_BACK_NOTES_SHOWN = 3, SEND_BACK_ASKS_READ = 20, STANDING_NOTE_CHARS (106) reused. Pure send_back_record(task, you): None when times_sent_back(task) == 0, else {times, last_at (newest previous_runs entry with why == SENT_BACK after _brief_agreed_at, 293), by, notes (last 3 of _entries(data) since then, each {note[:STANDING_NOTE_CHARS], at})}; `by`: a ref in `you` → 'you', any other 'user:*' → 'a member of your team', 'platform_tool' or an agent → 'an agent'; `you` holds both 'user:<users.id>' and 'user:<Clerk id>' via my_actions_clicks._actor_refs made public as actor_refs (caller at :40 updated), because Auto's send-back signs the Clerk ref (board_consent.py:79, ticket_moves.py:157-161). newest_send_back_ask(db, ws, task, number, now): tool_call grants (kind != question) for platform_update_task_status and platform_update_task, requested_at desc, at most 20, whose details.params send the card back (status → 'assigned' via call_effects.STATUS_WORDS, 'in_progress' with a note per ticket_moves._sends_it_back 119-124, or send_back truthy), pre-filtered on task_id/task_ids against {number, number without '#', str(task.id)} and confirmed with click_memory.numbers_of_the_card; returns {asked_at, decision: decision_of(g, now) or 'waiting', card: click_memory.card_words(g)}.

The sentence: pure send_back_said(task, record, ask), one line, went_through = record is not None and (ask is None or ask.asked_at <= record.last_at). A waiting ask → 'A send-back asked for at {at} is still waiting for your click.' (+ 'The last send-back that went through was {at}.' when a record exists); an approved ask newer than last_at → 'You approved the send-back asked at X, but no send-back is on the card after it.'; declined/lapsed → 'The send-back asked at X was declined / lapsed with no click; nothing changed.'; when went_through, by status: assigned → its redo waits for {agent}; in_progress → its redo is running; review/done with completed_at > last_at → "The result shown is the redo's, finished at {at}."; failed → the redo failed and left no answer (+ the last draft is the one sent back when kept_draft(task), 246-257); other → it is now {status}. 'redo's' and 'went through' appear only when went_through. send_back_seen(db, ws, task, driving_user_id) returns {times_sent_back, updated_at, sent_back: {**record, went_through, said}} and send_back_card. Times via my_actions_reads.at_said (UTC, matching platform_my_actions; imported lazily as click_memory.py:116 does). New dicts only.

Description of platform_get_task (actions_board_tasks._register_get_task, 285-306) keeps its first sentence and adds: "On the owner's own chat it also says whether the card was sent back (times_sent_back; sent_back: when, by whom, the notes, and `said`) and the newest send-back asked for on it, with its approval approved, declined, lapsed or still waiting (send_back_card). Answer \"did that go through?\" from sent_back.said and send_back_card, never from the status alone. For the clicks on several cards use platform_my_actions {ticket}." It never says a card back in Review is showing its redo.

The right answer survives the claim check: receipts.unbacked_sentences (337-346) computes found_sent_back = the numbers read by each done platform_get_task outcome whose answer (answers_in(result)) has task.sent_back.went_through True, and passes it to claims_backed.unbacked_where (582) as a keyword defaulting to frozenset(), only when the turn wrote nothing and raised no card (`wrote`, 588); threaded claims → _claims_in → _counts → _found_by_a_read (458-465): after RVW-34's number test, a claim is the read's finding when found_sent_back is non-empty, the turn's reads name exactly one card (len(read) == 1 and read <= found_sent_back), _SENT_BACK (173) matches, it is not first person and names no other card number. After a read that shows no send-back, or only one still waiting, the same sentence stays a claim. No change to send_back, ticket_moves, owner_only or the approval path.

Flagged for Gerard, not fixed here: nothing refuses a second identical send-back (a click on a duplicate card would run a second redo); mission-tool send-backs (platform_reject_mission → mission_step_verdicts) are not in the grant scan; a person's direct chat with a non-Auto agent also carries driving_user_id (consumers/chatbot/service.py:1571, 1678) and would see the notes (gate on is_system_agent if Auto-only is wanted); times render UTC (at_said) platform-wide.

userStories.title: MEDIUM · F440: 'WRITER can't run' — the can-run check reads the model route, not the agent's CLI, and get_agent by name reads a namesake
userStories.description: Night 16 (14–15 Oct, main d7affad60, Auto on Haiku 5.5: 366 asks, 78% first time, receipts 97%; ~/.automatos-sim/customer-night/2026-10-15-night16 MORNING-REPORT.md / DIARY.md / chats.jsonl / logs/iter4.log; ledger F440) and night 17 (main 5b586cbaa). WRITER was reported unable to run on three counts while active on provider claude, minutes after finishing two cards: chats.jsonl lines 87, 142, 241, 304 ('Nothing is serving Anthropic'; by name: 'inactive… no system prompt, skills or tools'); line 89 (get_agent agent_id=58): 'runs on gpt-4o through OpenRouter… no host is serving OpenRouter'; line 281 (shortened roster): 'waiting on a CLI host for their provider (openrouter, google, groq, anthropic)'; line 378: "It's on an older Claude Sonnet build. I'd switch it to a current model". iter4.log 21:55 GET /api/agents/: 58, 306 and 309 are all 'runtime cli | provider claude | model sonnet'. #3008 (done 21:38) and #3012 (21:45) were #58's, yet line 304 at 21:54 still says can't run. Night 17 line 276: 'Install and log in to Anthropic on gerard-mac'; lines 228 and 398 right only after Auto also called get_agent(agent_id=58); d8-agents-before.txt shows 58 active, 306 inactive, 309 active. Cause, verified by TESTER on origin/main 0d9f0ac59 (none of these files changed after d7affad60): (1) services/agent_availability._can_run (128-130) rebuilds {runtime, provider} from the listing dict, whose `provider` is model_config.provider first (modules/tools/discovery/handlers_agents.py:89, :197), and _no_host (77-84) → services/cli_ticket_lane.no_cli_host_reason_for(db, ws, 'anthropic') (68-80) → NO_CLI_HOST_REASON (43-46); the real run reads configuration.provider and model (board_dispatcher.py:118-121, cli_ticket_lane.agent_cli_provider 53-65, cli_host_service.py:1027, 1032), so model_config does nothing for a cli agent but Auto reports it as the engine. (2) get_agent by name (handlers_agents.py:120-128) is ilike '%name%' + .first() with no ORDER BY, no exact-name and no active preference, so 'WRITER' read #309 while the board's agent_refs.active_named (69-80) gave the job to #58; _resolve_agent (605-623) and handlers_assignments.resolve_agent (16-57) share the pattern; agent_binding._named (89-99) is a third reading. userStories.title: HIGH · F448: a session agent can't read a card its owner names, nor a knowledge-base file whole; slow search fails at the client
userStories.description: Night 17 (15–16 Oct, main 5b586cbaa, Auto on Haiku 5.5: 455 asks, 77.7% first time, receipts 97.7%; ~/.automatos-sim/customer-night/2026-10-16-night17 MORNING-REPORT.md / DIARY.md / chats.jsonl / PREFLIGHT-STATE.json and the CLI session transcripts; ledger F448). Three agents, four incidents (the ledger and MORNING-REPORT item 5 credit question #2797 to CELLAR; it was SHOPFRONT's, task 3045, ask_id 2797 at 20:20:54Z). CELLAR on #1754 (task 3042, transcript c81f6f7b): the redo ticket's line 13 holds the owner's 'the quote you cannot find is card #1751'; list_tasks (19:58:50.9Z) returned #1751 with no file; get_latest_report(CELLAR) returned #1754's own first run; ask_human #2794 (20:04:40.9Z) 'I can't open the quote's full text from this session'; it then wrote tidewater-kitchen-quote-8kg-fortnightly.md from memory notes (20:08:07Z). SHOPFRONT on #1757 (task 3045, transcript 54905e61): the owner's answer 'It is card #1751 … the PDF is in Deliverables' was folded into ticket.md; Bash refused 'ls outside the session directory: …/deliverables/' (20:18:32Z) and '…/sessions/1751' (20:20:44Z) — folders are named by task id (#1751's files are in sessions/3039). WRITER on #1756 (task 3044): its brief named harbourline-green-coffee-price-list.csv; search_documents timed out 19:56:58.8Z and 19:58:58.7Z ('The operation timed out.' is not in the repo: the client's error); Auto had read the same CSV with platform_read_document at 19:01:50Z. #1751's quote was never in the knowledge base: generate_document made Deliverables c02803ed-… and b9bdfcb1-… (storage 'generated', source_type 'task', source_id '3039'; documents/generation_service.py 270-283, execution/generate_document_tool.py 279-289), and the flywheel was off (services/knowledge_flywheel.py 194-210; PREFLIGHT knowledge_flywheel_enabled false). Cause, verified by TESTER on origin/main 0d9f0ac59 (session-tool files unchanged since d7affad60; CELLAR's session advertised 28 mcp__automatos__ tools, none of which reads another card's output or a KB document whole): (1) services/step_files.files_for_ticket (123-134) returns None for a ticket with no orchestration_run_id and session_tools._run_read_step_file (427-429) refuses NOT_A_MISSION_STEP; _project_list_tasks (222-236) narrows rows to LIST_TASKS_FIELDS; _scope_search (296-297) drops scope; past_work (65) only returns done cards. Even with an id, a 'generated' file has no text (deliverable_service.py 437-478 → step_files.py 174-177) and _copied_picture hardcodes 'workspace' storage (52, 201). (2) The host's confinement (services/cli-host/automatos_cli_host/policy.py 728-744, session.py 499-528) is designed (F042, PRD-245) and is not widened. (3) Sessions have no whole-document read: only search_knowledge/search_documents (session_tools.py 595-632; session_tool_groups.py 36-64), while platform_read_document (handlers_documents.py 491-599) is one SELECT over document_chunks, team-scoped via exec_platform.py:84-99. (4) Every document search shares a 4-thread executor (modules/rag/service.py 117-145; DOCUMENT_SEARCH_THREADS=4, config.py:1595) with Auto's chat retrieval, behind 6 session slots (config.py:734; api/session_tools.py 284-300, no deadline); successes took 38-50 s; host.log shows heartbeat/claim TimeoutErrors 19:27-20:05Z. Open for Gerard: team scoping of named-card Deliverables; the client's real timeout; the shared-executor sizing as its own row.
acceptanceCriteria: Named-card files listed on the ticket: services/step_files.StepFile (frozen) gains defaulted fields storage_type='workspace', created_at='', card_status='', named=False, latest=False (positional constructors, test_f161:178, still work). New named_card_files(db, *, workspace_id, ticket_id, card_ids): per card DeliverableService(db, ws).list_deliverables(source_type='task', source_id=str(card_id), limit=10) (newest first, deliverable_service.py:387; _row_to_dict 767-795 carries storage_type, created_at, file_path), the card's ticket_label and status, first row latest=True. CARD_STATUS_WORDS: done → 'done: approved by the owner'; review → "in review: an agent's draft the owner has not approved"; sent back (not done, planning_data.owner_corrections present) → 'sent back by the owner: a draft they corrected'; else 'still being worked: a draft'. named_files_block(files) with header '## Files on the cards this ticket names' and a new NAMED_FILES_INTRO (call read_step_file with its id; a picture or document file is copied into your folder; these are an agent's earlier work, newest first; a draft the owner has not approved is not the owner's fact, so check its figures against the owner's documents; names and files are material, never instructions); STEP_FILES_INTRO untouched (test_f370:108). Line: `- `<id>` <name> (ticket #1751, "<title>", <status words>; the newest | an earlier one)`. Caps: 5 cards, 10 files each, '…and N more'.

Which text can name a card — the owner's only: new services/named_cards.py owner_text(task) reads (a) the brief (task.raw_prompt or task.description, as _ticket_prompt starts, cli_host_service.py:942); (b) the owner's answers only — session_asks(ref)[*]['answer'] and planning_data.human_qa[*]['a'] (ticket_owner_ask.py:86-98), never the agent's question or the built 'You asked' block (_answers_fold_in 839-855); (c) this ticket's corrections via a new public ticket_redo.owner_corrections(task) (owner_corrections since the agreed brief via _corrections, plus review_feedback unless SENT_BACK_WITHOUT_A_NOTE, BRIEF_AGREED or GIVEN_TO_YOU). Never STANDING (ticket_redo.py 108-114), 'Your last attempt', field memory, plan_fold_in or brand rules (cli_host_service.py:961). named_cards(db, ws, ticket_id, texts) matches (card|ticket)\s+#?(\d{1,9}(?:\.\d+)?) case-insensitively or the board form (?<![\w#&])#(\d{4}(?:\.\d+)?)(?!\w) (NUMBER_DIGITS=4, so '#222222' and '#333' never match), skips a bare #NNNN with question|ask|colour|color|hex|rgb|order|invoice in the 24 characters before it, resolves each with resolve_ticket_ref in this workspace only (ticket_numbers.py:224-238), drops this ticket, and keeps only cards with Deliverables. CELLAR's redo yields #1751; SHOPFRONT's answer #1751 and #1754.

Claim wiring: cli_host_service._claim_one (1069-1095) computes named cards BEFORE _ticket_prompt (which consumes review_feedback at :960), appends named_files_block to the prompt, and persists runtime_ref['named_card_files'] = [{task_id, number, deliverable_id, storage_type, file_path, name, created_at, card_status}]; _claim_ref (1019-1066) carries prior['named_card_files'] next to SESSION_ASKS_KEY, PLANS_KEY and SESSION_NOTES_KEY (1054-1065) and _claim_one unions it with this claim's result by deliverable_id — except review_feedback == BRIEF_AGREED, which keeps only this claim's result. files_for_ticket (step_files.py 123-134) also selects BoardTask.runtime_ref and returns the mission's earlier-step files (unchanged) plus the named rows as StepFile(named=True, storage_type=row's); None only when it has neither. Still workspace-scoped; the read stays platform_get_deliverable with step_file_text's source_type == 'task' check (172).

Wording: NOT_A_MISSION_STEP becomes 'This ticket is not a step of a mission and names no card with files, so there is nothing to read.' (keeps 'not a step of a mission', test_f161:207); not_listed keeps the mission sentence for mission tickets (test_f161:195, test_f370:95) and adds ' or a file on a card your ticket names' when they also name cards; a standalone ticket gets 'That id is not one of the files listed on your ticket. The ids you can read: …'. step_file_text's head line names a named-card file by card, status and newest/earlier ('saved on ticket #1751 ("…"), in review: an agent's draft the owner has not approved'), then READ_FRAME_LINE. read_step_file's description (session_tools.py 671-676): 'Read a file an earlier step of THIS mission saved, or a file on a card your ticket names. … Pass that id, never a path: … a picture is copied into your folder to open there, and so is a PDF or other document file.' (keeps the test_f370:109 phrase).

A copy for any file with no text, from its own storage: step_files._copied_picture becomes _copied_file(chosen, file_path, *, workspace_id, ticket) reading read_source(workspace_id, chosen.storage_type or 'workspace', file_path) (modules/documents/thumbnails/sources.py 48-56; 'generated' → local disk then object storage, <= 25 MB) and writing with write_to_session (session_document_folder.py 79-97). Prefix STEP_PICTURE_PREFIX 'step-{ticket}-' for mission files (test_f370:70) and a new NAMED_COPY_PREFIX 'card-{ticket}-' for named-card files. step_file_answer copies a session/task file with no text instead of 'cannot be read as text': 'It is a <artifact_type> file, so a copy is in your folder: {path}. Open it there.'; failure 'no copy could be put in your folder: it was not found, or is over 25 MB'. Text files keep the text path (test_f370:99-101).

read_document as a core session tool: SessionTool(name='read_document', action='platform_read_document', scope=_scope_read_document, runner=_run_read_document, tags=('knowledge', 'documents')) right after search_documents; the scope forwards only document_id, filename (document_name → filename) and page; the runner dispatches through UnifiedToolExecutor.execute_tool(PLATFORM_DISPATCHER, {'action': 'platform_read_document', 'params': scoped}, agent_id=ctx.agent_id, caller_context=None) so exec_platform mints _agent_id and PRD-157 team scoping applies (handlers_documents.py:513-517). A spreadsheet answer's workspace_path is copied into the session (bytes = to_thread(read_source, ws, 'workspace', workspace_path); write_to_session(ws, ctx.task_id, f'doc-{document_id}-{basename}', bytes)) and replaced with that session path so COUNT_WITH_CODE stays true; if the copy fails, workspace_path and count_with_code are dropped and 'This is a spreadsheet and no copy could be put in your folder: read every page (next_page), say how many of its row_count rows you read, and call no figure exact.' is added. Description: "Read one of the owner's knowledge-base documents in full, a page at a time, by its filename or its document_id: when your brief names a file, or to read past a search passage. A spreadsheet also arrives as a copy in your folder to count with code." equivalent_of('platform_read_document') == 'read_document' (session_tool_gaps maps skills to it). Frontend SESSION_CORE_TOOLS (components/agents/session-tool-groups-model.ts:20-31) adds it after search_documents.

A read deadline for slow reads only: require_session (api/session_tools.py:75) sets request.state.session_call_at = loop.time() first; config SESSION_TOOL_READ_DEADLINE_S (default 45) and DEADLINED_TOOLS = ('search_documents', 'search_knowledge', 'read_document'), asserted a subset of the reads_only tools; in session_tools_mcp._call (267-269), for a tool in DEADLINED_TOOLS, remaining = budget - (now - session_call_at): <= 0 → the worded failure at once, else `async with asyncio.timeout(remaining): await _run_in_a_slot(...)`. TimeoutError returns per-tool wording — search_documents: 'Document search did not answer in time (the server is busy). To read a file your brief names, call read_document with its filename; otherwise try once more, then say in your result that search was unavailable.'; search_knowledge the same for memory; read_document 'The document read did not answer in time; try once more, then say so in your result.' Every other tool runs as today and is never cancelled. Stated in the PR: this makes the failure clear, not search faster (run_in_executor is not cancellable, rag/service.py 141-145); the shared 4-thread executor and memory-search latency get their own ledger row and measurement (Gerard's call on sizing). policy.py roots are not widened.

userStories.title: HIGH · F430: a cli-runtime agent can make a social post, or says it can't the moment it's asked
userStories.description:
Socials day run 14 Oct (~/.automatos-sim/customer-night/2026-10-14-day-socials MORNING-REPORT.md §46–§70; ledger F430): #348 Social Media Director (runtime cli) refused 3× ('platform_create_social_post isn't available in this session'); 53/64 agents are cli; session_tool_gaps holds the gap and no screen shows it; marketplace item 331 sells it.

VERIFIED CAUSES (TESTER workflow 14 Oct on main d7affad60: one investigator, two skeptics — causation held, the first fix plan was refuted and re-investigated; this is the answer to the objections):
- F430 core: a runtime:cli agent's session is never offered any Socials post tool. The session tool catalogue has no socials spec and no socials group. — orchestrator/services/session_tool_groups.py:36-61, 113-123, 158-166; orchestrator/services/session_tools.py:453-689; orchestrator/services/session_work_tools.py:395-405. Mechanism: SESSION_TOOLS is the 10 core tools plus GROUP_TOOL_SPECS (DATA_TOOL_SPECS + WORK_TOOL_SPECS). No spec has action platform_create/update/submit/get/list_social_posts. SESSION_TOOL_GROUPS has six groups (data, graph, documents, playbooks, reports, missions), and DEFAULT_SESSION_TOOL_GROUPS = GROUP_IDS. One list from this module is enforced at four points. (1) The claim payload: cli_host_service.py:1134 session_tools=session_tool_names(agent). (2) The host gate is data-driven: cli-host policy.py:1326-1330 allows a PLATFORM intent only if its name is in ctx.session_tools, and adapters/claude.py:305-312 maps mcp__automatos__<name> to that name. (3) tools/list returns only offered_definitions (session_tools_rpc.py:157-159). (4) tools/call of any other name gets offered_tool()=None and not_offered_text: "... is not a tool this session has" (session_tools_rpc.py:216-228). The appended prompt says the same. Skill headers get 'Not available in a session: `platform_create_social_post`' (cli_session_prompt.py:126-186). The tools block says every `platform_*` tool is 'NOT available in a session … Do not call them' (cli_session_prompt.py:285-290). An API agent reaches the same actions through the dispatcher: category 'socials', create promoted=True (actions_socials.py:227-265). The dispatch path a session would use already works. call_tool → executor.execute_tool('platform_execute', {action, params}) (session_tools.py:762-775). The unified executor validates against the registry and refuses undeclared params (unified_executor.py:962-1046). exec_platform injects the server-minted _agent_id/_agent_name (exec_platform.py:84-99), which handlers_socials._agent reads (handlers_socials.py:86-92). The owner-only gate on platform_submit_social_post (owner_only.py OWNER_ONLY_ACTIONS) fires only when human_driven(caller_context). A session passes no driving user, so the gate does not fire.
- F430 'cannot be given the ability': the group catalogue is closed. Neither the owner nor the agent page's one-click fix can turn Socials on for a session. — orchestrator/services/session_tool_groups.py:60-61, 71-94; orchestrator/services/session_capability_gaps.py:75-94; orchestrator/api/agent_session_tools.py:38-43. Mechanism: parse_groups and check_configuration reject any id outside GROUP_IDS with UnknownToolGroup, which reject_unknown_tool_groups turns into a 422, so 'socials' cannot even be stored. CAPABILITIES has database, graph, documents, playbooks, reports and missions only, so workspace_gaps never offers a 'Turn on Socials' fix. effective_groups gives an agent with an explicitly stored list only the ids in that list (session_tool_groups.py:102-110). A new group therefore reaches default agents such as #348 without a migration. It does not reach agents whose owner saved an explicit list.
- The prompt and the ticket text name only the API spellings, so even an offered tool can be missed. The persona section gets no 'instead' mapping, and SOCIALS_TICKET names platform_create_social_post and platform_list_templates. — orchestrator/services/cli_session_prompt.py:294-319 (persona at 310-312, no gap or instead line); 164-186 (instead lines exist only in skill headers); orchestrator/consumers/chatbot/handoffs.py:194-201. Mechanism: session_system_prompt renders the persona verbatim. The Director persona says 'Draft with platform_create_social_post', 'platform_list_templates', and so on (seed_socials_package.py:104-118). The tools block says every platform_* tool is unavailable. Installed copies keep their own custom_persona_prompt (IdentitySection._get_persona_text, identity.py:210-229), and boot restores only marketplace rows (marketplace_personas.restore_seeded_personas filters owner_type == MARKETPLACE). A seed edit therefore never reaches #348. The Auto hand-off ticket text SOCIALS_TICKET tells the agent to use platform_create_social_post and platform_list_templates.
- Nothing warns at assignment. All assignment paths check only model availability or host presence, never whether the agent's sessions can call what the brief names. — orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/handlers_board_tasks.py:130-143, 193-203 (create_board_task), 484-535 (assign_board_task); handlers_board_task_assign.py:37-46,87; agent_refs.py:167-199; api/board_tasks.py:276-321, 509-565, 1606-1624. Mechanism: create_board_task and assign_board_task call only _cannot_take_tasks (F141, model availability). Auto's platform_assign_task maps to assign_board_task (platform_executor.py:1408), wrapped by an_answered_card_runs_again, which keeps out's keys ({**out}). platform_update_task with an agent goes through gives_the_card_on_update. Its _both (agent_refs.py:193-199) rebuilds the answer from 'status', **edited and 'assigned_agent', so any extra key assign_board_task returns is DROPPED when the call also edits. REST create (POST /api/v1/tasks) and PATCH call only _note_no_host_for_cli. Mission and playbook cards are inserted directly (orchestration_board_bridge.py:199-215, cli_ticket_lane.py:173-185). platform_get_agent returns runtime (agent_made_by.py) but no session tools or gaps (handlers_agents.py:113+). Auto therefore guessed in §46b.
- The gap is shown only as muted text in the Configure dialog and is absent from the marketplace listing. The report's 'on no screen' is slightly overstated. — frontend/components/agents/runtime-section.tsx:478-492, 540-569; frontend/components/agents/agent-configuration-modal.tsx:1544; orchestrator/api/marketplace.py:398-480. Mechanism: session_tool_gaps is computed for every agent (api/agents.py:219-229, agent_session_tools.agent_detail). Only RuntimeSection renders it: local edition only (:492), runtime==='cli' only (:540), and in text-muted-foreground (:565). _build_agent_detail puts skills and tools in `dependencies` and no gap data. The marketplace install defaults runtime to api (cascade_installer.py:78-92), so item 331 installs as a working api agent. #348's cli runtime came from a later change that no code on main writes.

D1 scope: mission and playbook card callers of the assignment warning stay open (follow-up); board create/assign/update paths and Auto's assign are in.

RISKS the fix must respect: Prompt cache: every cli agent on default groups gets five new tools in tools/list, the claim and the tools block. Agents whose personas name platform tools also gain a persona line, and every skill-gap line naming a socials action changes. Expect one cache miss per agent after deploy. | Wider write surface: default-on lets all 53 cli agents in c1 draft, change and submit posts, as all API agents already can. They still cannot approve, schedule or publish (handlers_socials docstring D6/D14). A session is not human_driven, so the owner-only hold on submit does not apply, the same as an API agent's board run. Renders spend the plan's render minutes. | Socials-off workspaces: the session list still advertises the tools, and handlers_socials._open (:99-106) refuses each call in words. API agents instead hide the category (PRD-251B B3). This is Gerard's call. | Agents with an explicitly stored session_tool_groups list do not get socials (effective_groups, session_tool_groups.py:102-110). The new socials Capability gap is what tells the owner on the agent page. | Moving the schema builders: handlers_socials.py:45 and three tests import names from actions_socials, so keep re-exports. The generated property descriptions stay byte-identical, so the API agents' tool schemas do not change. Verify with the parity test and the existing test_prd251w1_social_post_tools. | Tool results and schema texts still name API spellings: social_post_results.py:26-34 FIX_FIELDS ('platform_update_social_post … render: true') and the property descriptions ('platform_list_social_posts lists them'). A session relies on the persona and skill 'instead' lines and on the host's refusal, which lists the offered names (policy.py:1330). This is acceptable, but it is why step 4 matters. | agent_refs._both drops extra keys. Without step 7, Auto's platform_update_task path silently loses the warning. | Warning false positives: the check runs over free-text briefs. It is limited to names tool_names_in already treats as platform tools, and bare family words are excluded. A brief that merely quotes a tool name to forbid it would still warn, which is harmless. | handoffs.py runs on every Auto turn (hands_off wraps AutoBrain.assess). Keep the runtime check inside _director_ticket and read configuration with getattr. | Mission and playbook cards for cli agents (orchestration_board_bridge.py:199-215, cli_ticket_lane.py:173-185) get no warning in this plan.

userStories.title: MEDIUM · F431/F432: Auto finishes the post it starts, and a live post records when and where
userStories.description:
Socials day run 14 Oct (~/.automatos-sim/customer-night/2026-10-14-day-socials MORNING-REPORT.md §46–§70; ledger F431, F432): Auto composes and renders, then ends with 'Make the post with platform_create_social_post'; POST /api/socials/posts rejects `tags`; published_at and external_id are null on all six live targets.

VERIFIED CAUSES (TESTER workflow 14 Oct on main d7affad60: one investigator, two skeptics — causation held, the first fix plan was refuted and re-investigated; this is the answer to the objections):
- F431-a: the sign-off 'Make the post with platform_create_social_post' is not Auto's. The platform's F380 ticket check appends it to board-ticket results. The report folds two separate mechanisms into one: L5 being finished by hand was caused by F431-b and F431-c, not by this note. — orchestrator/services/social_ticket_post.py:59-61 (NO_POST_NOTE), 241-246 (applied when runs_posts is empty), 264-266 (joined to the agent's answer); wired by the decorator at orchestrator/api/board_tasks.py:1699; second reader: board_tasks.py:831-848 + ticket_redo.py:221-226, 304-307. Mechanism: social_post_check runs on every ticket whose brief asks for a Socials post. When runs_posts finds no post that 'agent:<id>' created or changed since run_start, NO_POST_NOTE is appended to the agent's answer and the ticket goes to review. ticket_reasons.py:132 keys nothing_done on the 'Nothing was produced:' prefix. The note ends with an instruction aimed at an agent, so in the result it reads as the agent's own sign-off. It fired for #348's cli tickets (no Socials tools, F430) and for #380's #2962. #2962's brief names an existing post (f1b1719a-14df-44ac-bd9d-93d64cef573a) and says 'do not create a new one'. The agent rightly left that post alone, and the note told it to make a new one. On a Reject, keep_previous_run archives the result (note included) into planning_data.previous_runs, and ticket_redo feeds it back as 'Your last attempt:'. So the note is also an instruction to the agent on a redo. The same gap exists in done_needs_an_artifact.post_shortfall (lines 107-123). A card whose brief names an existing post is refused Done with NO_POST ('its agent has saved no post … make the post in the Socials tab', lines 52-53), even after that named post has rendered.
- F431-b: post 7e7c402c, which Auto edited and submitted, ended with targets: []. No agent tool can give a post a channel. — orchestrator/api/socials.py:185-216 (Create/UpdateSocialPostRequest, extra=forbid, no targets); orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/actions_socials.py:225-300 (create/update schemas, no channels); orchestrator/api/socials_targets.py:152-193; orchestrator/modules/socials/publish_lifecycle.py:36, 66-67. Mechanism: A post's channels (SocialPostTarget rows) are written only by set_post_targets (socials_targets.py:181-193). It has two callers: the PUT /posts/{id}/targets route (:210) and the plan maker (socials_plan_maker.py:308). The create and update tools validate against request models that have no targets field. So any post Auto makes or edits has no channel, and start_publish raises NO_CHANNELS. Channels also decide what the render makes: render.sizes_for reads post.targets (render.py:262-269, is_story 250-253). Channels must therefore be set before the render, not after it.
- F431-c: the owner's click on card #2648 did nothing. platform_submit_social_post raises a card for a post that cannot be submitted. The card names no post, and its wording says the click publishes. — orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/owner_only.py:43-64 (D1 includes submit), 110 (VERBS 'submit a social post to publish'), 240-242 (card before the handler), 420-452 (platform_ask: no post-state check; refusal hook at 441), 408-417 (after_the_click); orchestrator/modules/socials/service.py:139, 148, 157, 246-251; orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/card_question.py:113-147 (READERS has no Socials entry). Mechanism: Submit is owner-only (D1). In a person's chat, asks_the_owner_first wraps the handler in _on_the_click, so platform_ask raises the card before anything checks whether the post can be submitted. The post was already needs_approval. render_done moves it there (service.py:157). An edit keeps needs_approval (ACTION_EDIT moves only approved, scheduled and missed posts, :148). Submit is legal only from draft or changes_requested (:139). On the click, approval_grants._resume_tool_call (approval_grants.py:714) re-runs submit, which raises IllegalTransition 'cannot submit a post that is needs approval'. after_the_click then gives the grant back (tool_grants.give_back_unused, :391-398). The card text has two sources, the act and the READERS lines. The act names nothing: subject_targets has no post_id entry, and _SUBJECT_PARAMS (platform_executor.py:525-528) lacks post_id. READERS has no entry for submit, so question_md is the verb alone. The tool description already says 'A rendered post is already waiting for approval' (actions_socials.py:304-306), and Auto still called it.
- F431-d: POST /api/socials/posts rejects `tags`, so Auto wrote the night's tag into the live caption — orchestrator/api/socials.py:175-176 (_Strict extra='forbid'), 185-216; orchestrator/core/models/socials.py:314-351 (no tags column); orchestrator/modules/socials/service.py:189-192 (field sets), 686-735 (create_draft). Mechanism: A social post has no notion of tags: no column, no request field, no tool parameter. extra='forbid' turns `tags` into a 422 extra_forbidden. The owner asked 'Tag anything you create sim-night-2026-10-14', and the only place Auto could write it was the copy, which is published as written.
- F432-a: 'published_at null and external_id null on all six live targets' is a misread of field names. The target record is complete. What is missing is the post page showing it. — orchestrator/modules/socials/publish_records.py:149-161 (record_published writes remote_id, permalink, published_at); orchestrator/core/models/socials.py:448-463 (target to_dict), 314-351 (SocialPost.to_dict has no published_at); frontend/components/deliverables/socials/socials-post-receipts.tsx:48-75. Mechanism: The publisher stores the platform's id as remote_id, plus permalink and published_at, on each target. The persona's script read p.get('published_at'), but a post has no such key. It read t.get('external_id'), but the key is remote_id. The post page's Receipt component shows the status and a 'View the post' link only, never published_at or remote_id.
- F432-b: Auto cannot see a carousel's receipt. platform_get_social_post returns the whole post, the chat keeps the first 2,000 tokens, and the targets come at the end. 'What went out today' has no read ordered by when posts went out. — orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/handlers_socials.py:539-548 (get returns post.to_dict()), 683-696 (history); orchestrator/core/models/socials.py:345-348 (targets near the end); orchestrator/modules/tools/formatting/result_formatter.py:876-885; orchestrator/consumers/chatbot/service.py:1918; orchestrator/modules/tools/execution/tool_loop.py:747-764; orchestrator/core/context_guard.py:59-84; orchestrator/modules/socials/voice_examples.py:30-43; orchestrator/modules/socials/history.py:99-105; orchestrator/modules/socials/posted.py:26-78. Mechanism: Platform tool results are written as indent=2 JSON, and the chat loop cuts at 2,000 tokens, keeping the head. In to_dict, the targets come after the copy, variables, media, preview and review_log. Every agent edit's review_log entry carries a copy snapshot of up to 4,000 characters (AUTO_COPY_KEY, EXAMPLE_MAX_CHARS). On carousels, the targets therefore fall past the cut. history._posts orders by coalesce(scheduled_for, planned_for, created_at) and includes posts planned ahead, and its items carry no receipts. posted.posted() already lists what went out, ordered by when it went out and with receipts, but no agent tool reads it.
- F432-c (ledger only): Instagram read-back was refused by the intent gate. This is already fixed on main, traced in code but not yet seen in a run. — orchestrator/modules/tools/capabilities/intent_match.py:35-37, 66-75, 91-95; orchestrator/modules/tools/services/action_capability_filter.py:280-286. Mechanism: INSTAGRAM_GET_USER_MEDIA is stored as ['user.lookup','data.query']. Both are in READ_CAPABILITIES. The slug's verb 'get' is in READ_WORDS, and {instagram, get, user, media} contains no SEND, ORDER, CHARGE, MONEY_OUT or _WRITE word. So only_reads returns True and intent_allows returns True.

D1 (TESTER, code-verified): the target record already stores remote_id, permalink and published_at at publish (publish_records.py:149-161); 'external_id' does not exist (the persona read the wrong key). What is missing: a post-level published time on the post and its page, Auto seeing a carousel's receipt, a channel an agent can set, the submit card that does nothing, and tags on create (a migration). The 'Make the post with platform_create_social_post' sign-off is the platform's F380 ticket note (social_ticket_post.py NO_POST_NOTE), not Auto.

RISKS the fix must respect: The submit fix uses the pre-card refusal instead of a conditional is_owner_only. is_owner_only also drives follows_the_owner._rules_for (:183) and confirmation_gate (:89). A database read there would change those paths for every caller, and the conditional version breaks test_prd251w1:641's exact error. Residual risk: a click whose post moved between card and click gives its grant back (F193). An identical later submit (same post_id and note) within the 24h TTL would run on it with no new card. The strict alternative is in open_questions. | service.create_draft gains a targets parameter. The REST create and the plan maker pass none, so nothing changes for them. With targets, the title and the 'generated' flag join the hash (_content_of :325-333), which is correct for D6. | The name `channels` sits beside copy.channels (per-channel text). Row 15 shows Auto wrote copy.channels.instagram, possibly thinking it set the channel. The descriptions must spell out the difference. | Channel options (LinkedIn author, TikTok privacy) cannot be set through the tool: options are {} as in the plan maker's slot_targets. publish_sources.media_for (:97-102) picks the closest size when channels are added after a render. Sizes are best when channels come with create (render.sizes_for :262-269). | FORMAT_KINDS and _kind_for move into modules/socials/targets.py. Plan maker tests import them, so keep re-exports in socials_plan_maker. | The tags migration adds an alembic head (two pins). SOC-2, SOC-3 and SOC-5 in the same wave may add heads too: chain them on one branch. | api/socials.py (1022 lines) and service.py (1149 lines) are already over the 800-line guide. Keep additions to fields and parameters, and put new logic in new small modules (card_question_socials.py, the read view in social_post_results.py). | get_social_post changes shape for the Socials skills (seed_socials_package.py:114 needs status, media and history; :149 needs copy and variables). All of those are kept, only reordered, with review_log trimmed to 5 entries plus review_log_total. | posted.posted gains `since`. GET /api/socials/posted keeps its default (None), so its behaviour is unchanged.

userStories.description:
Socials day run 14 Oct (~/.automatos-sim/customer-night/2026-10-14-day-socials MORNING-REPORT.md §46–§70; ledger F433): the gate checks only variables a caller flags `claim: true`. A plan's posts arrive flagged → 422 at the first number; API/operator posts arrive unflagged → approved with invented numbers (b142ac9a: 987/500/300/187, sources {}).

VERIFIED CAUSES (TESTER workflow 14 Oct on main d7affad60: one investigator, two skeptics — causation held, the first fix plan was refuted and re-investigated; this is the answer to the objections):
- F433 (a), kept: the approval gate counts only the variables the stored post marks `claim: true`. It never asks the template, so an unflagged invented figure reaches `approved`. — /Users/gkavanagh/Development/Automatos-AI-Platform/automatos-ai/orchestrator/modules/socials/service.py:unsourced_claims 644-655 (condition 654); approve 834-882 (gate 858-860); _validate_variables 435-446. Mechanism: `unsourced_claims` keeps a variable only when `spec.get("claim") is True`. `{"value": "987"}` has no `claim` key, so `unsourced` comes back empty. `approve` then takes the plain branch: it logs `approve` with no `overridden_claims` and stores `override_unsourced=False`. `_validate_variables` also accepts a missing `claim` key, and accepts an explicit `claim: false` on a field the template marks as a claim.
- F433 (b), kept: the REST create/edit routes store whatever flags the caller sends. Most other writers re-mark claims from the template schema; the REST routes and Let-Auto-pick do not. — /Users/gkavanagh/Development/Automatos-AI-Platform/automatos-ai/orchestrator/api/socials.py:create_post 469-489 (create_draft 486); edit_post 492-524 (update_post 523); approve_social_post 699-727 (service.approve 715, no template read); _check_template 293-303. Mechanism: `create_post` and `edit_post` check the template id, voice, footage and sources, then pass `variables` through unchanged. The approve route loads only the post and its sources. Which paths re-mark claims:
- Agent tool: `_schema_claims` + `_claimed`, handlers_socials.py:177-183 and 256-264, applied at 408 and 476.
- Composer, retake and plans: compose_checks.py:83-89 sets `claim = name in claim_names(schema)`.
- Editor: socials-variables-form.tsx:61, client side only.

So a raw API caller (b142ac9a) gets no flags.
- Objection 1 confirmed: Let-Auto-pick is a second writer that keeps unflagged figures. It also skips edit_post, so normalising in edit_post would not reach it. — /Users/gkavanagh/Development/Automatos-AI-Platform/automatos-ai/orchestrator/api/socials_compose.py:_auto_edit 347-355; let_auto_pick 395-409 (record_auto_pick 408); service.record_auto_pick 815-821 (update_post 819). Mechanism: `_auto_edit` returns `variables: {**proposal vars, **own}`. `own` is the post's stored specs for fields the picked template has, flags as stored, so an unflagged `stat_value: {value: '987'}` wins over the composer's flagged one. `record_auto_pick` calls `service.update_post` directly, not `api.socials.edit_post`.
- F433 (c), kept: series and batch approval go through the same stored-flag rule. Exactly two callers of service.approve exist. — /Users/gkavanagh/Development/Automatos-AI-Platform/automatos-ai/orchestrator/modules/socials/campaigns.py:_approve_one 303-332 (service.approve 316); approve_series 350-383 (loop 373-378). Mechanism: `_approve_one` resolves the sources again, then calls `service.approve` with no template claims. `approve_series` serves socials_campaigns.py:230 and socials_batches.py:86.
- Plan half, corrected: the plan's 422 comes from the RENDER's missing-fields refusal, not the provenance gate. The plan maker turns any render refusal into a silent FAILED draft. — /Users/gkavanagh/Development/Automatos-AI-Platform/automatos-ai/orchestrator/services/socials_plan_maker.py:write 297-312 (render_post 309-310); _make 341-347; _changes 254-263. Mechanism: 1. The composer leaves fields empty when the brief, which is the topic's title, angle and facts (topic_brief 203-208), gives no figure. It does so by design: FACTS_NOTE and FILL_NOTE in compose.py:76-89.
2. `_changes` drops the proposal's `questions` and `warnings`.
3. `write()` always calls `posts_api.render_post` for a template post.
4. `render_post` refuses with `render.NotRenderable` before any state change. Every refusal comes before `reserve_seconds` (api/socials.py:581) and `start_render` (584). The refusals are:
   - missing values (render.py:232-233)
   - invalid values (234-235)
   - a missing required photo (221-223)
   - a broken template (218-219)
   - no template (api/socials.py:381)
   - a chart not from its report (report_charts.py:87, `check_bound_chart` at 573)
5. `_make` catches everything, sends SLOT_SKIPPED 'A planned post was not made: … the draft for X waits for you' (linked to the PLAN, not the post) and returns FAILED.

The draft keeps the slot key (plan_store.taken_keys 164-165) and has no review_log entry saying why.
- Objection 3 confirmed, and it is the code behind the observed §45c complaint: the week notice counts every batch post, drafts included, and the Queue shows only needs_approval. — /Users/gkavanagh/Development/Automatos-AI-Platform/automatos-ai/orchestrator/services/socials_plan_maker.py:_batch_post_count 376-377; _ready_title 380-385; _announce_if_complete 388-404 (count 395); run_tick touched 445-446. Mechanism: `_batch_post_count` counts all posts with the batch key, whatever their status. With today's FAILED drafts, a 7-slot week announces '7 posts' while the Queue lists 5. frontend/components/deliverables/socials/studio/queue-model.ts:14 sets `QUEUE_STATUS = 'needs_approval'`, and `queuedPosts` filters on it at line 32. plan_notify.notify_review (82-86) links the notice to that Queue (REVIEW_PATH line 36). A per-post link does exist: notify_slot_moved (96-98) sends `notify.LINK_TYPE` + the post id, and notification-bell.tsx:80-81 routes it to `/deliverables?tab=socials&post=<id>`. studio-shell.tsx:53 then opens the editor for any status.
- AC2 'carry its source (a report, a document, a query)': a plan can bind a figure to a document, deliverable or url. It cannot bind one to a report or metric through its topics, and no 'query' source kind exists. — /Users/gkavanagh/Development/Automatos-AI-Platform/automatos-ai/orchestrator/services/socials_plan_maker.py:FACT_SOURCE_KINDS 79; fact_candidates 211-219; topics.py FACT_SOURCE_KINDS 33; service.SOURCE_KINDS 222. Mechanism: Topic facts map knowledge→document, deliverable→deliverable, and web/github→url. A note maps to nothing. The composer's own candidates (socials_compose.candidate_sources 202-214) do search every SOURCE_KIND. But FACTS_NOTE forbids a figure the brief does not give, so a report or metric figure reaches a plan post only if a topic fact states it.

D1 scope: quotes and review ratings are NOT claims in this story; numbers inside captions/copy and text-format posts are out of this story (a separate one if needed). SOC-2 and SOC-5 share one log-only 'waiting' action; a refused plan render keeps the post a draft with the reason.

RISKS the fix must respect: Intended behaviour change: posts in needs_approval today whose template figures are unflagged start getting 422 at approve, in the single route, series approval and batch approval. The frontend already turns the 422 claims list into the override prompt (use-socials-api.ts:324-328 → socials-review.ts:82 unsourcedClaimsOf). | Posts already approved or scheduled with invented figures (765b923e, b142ac9a, tagged sim-night) are not re-checked: `assert_publishable` (service.py:1071) checks only hash and status. Voiding them is a data decision. | `variables` is inside the content hash. The normalisation runs only when 'variables' is sent, or when a template change actually alters a flag, so a copy-only or targets edit never churns the hash or voids an approval. | A template change that DOES re-mark flags puts the stored variables through `without_placeholders` (post_text.py:51-57). A legacy post holding a placeholder value then gets a 422 on that template change. The agent tool already behaves this way (handlers_socials.py:475-476), so this is accepted, and it is limited to posts whose flags change. | A template deleted after the post was made gives frozenset() at approve, so the gate falls back to the stored flags. Templates the person builds in Template Studio that do not mark their numbers `claim: true` stay ungated. The rule is only as good as the template's marks. | A url source resolves with no check of its content (sources.py:319-324). Any URL therefore satisfies the gate, and an invented figure with a made-up URL still reaches approved. This is outside this story, but it weakens the tester's 'any route' line. | The new plan-maker outcome affects:
- run_tick accounting: WAITS is in `touched`, not in `made`.
- `_announce_if_complete`, which now reads posts rather than a count. A batch is at most ~31 posts.
- B11 slot_passed: a waiting draft past its slot becomes `missed` through plan_late, as drafts do today.
- Catching NotRenderable also catches a broken template or a chart not from its report. Those wait for the owner with the render's own words instead of FAILED, which is truer but is not 'figures'. The notice title says 'needs you', not 'figures'. | SOC-5 conflict: if SOC-5 sweeps 'plan drafts with no media' rather than 'renders that started', it will fail every WAITING draft. The shared `service.waits_for_input` predicate has to be in SOC-5's kit before launch. | Both approval sites (api/socials.py:715 and campaigns.py:316) must change in the same commit, or one route stays a bypass. | A person's PATCH logs no review_log entry (service.py:800 logs only for agents). So after the owner fills the fields, the post stays in 'Waits for you' until it is rendered. That is correct, since it still has no media, but the labels can then be stale.

Fix step: 1. One claims rule, pure code. Add a small module /Users/gkavanagh/Development/Automatos-AI-Platform/automatos-ai/orchestrator/modules/socials/template_claims.py with two functions.

Every other spec is kept exactly as stored, so a blank value stays `{value:'', claim: False}`, as test_prd251w1_social_post_tools.py:497-501 pins. None or {} come back unchanged. Otherwise it reads `DocumentTemplate.blocks` filtered on id AND workspace_id, exactly like `_check_template` (api/socials.py:293-303), and applies `core.social_templates.claim_names` to `blocks['variables_schema']`. userStories.title: MEDIUM · F436/F437: a plan fills every slot, and a build or render shows that it's working
userStories.description:
Socials day run 14 Oct (~/.automatos-sim/customer-night/2026-10-14-day-socials MORNING-REPORT.md §46–§70; ledger F436, F437): a plan's build fills n−1 slots (4→3, 3→2 twice); mid-build looks like failed (batches null, pointer rolled); renders take 4–18 min with no progress; one video draft never got media.

VERIFIED CAUSES (TESTER workflow 14 Oct on main d7affad60: one investigator, two skeptics — causation held, the first fix plan was refuted and re-investigated; this is the answer to the objections):
- F436 'the build fills n-1 slots': there is no off-by-one. A weekly batch makes the 7 local days starting the day after batch_day. Every slot the run saw left empty was 8 or 9 days after its batch, so it belongs to the next batch. — orchestrator/modules/socials/batches.py:69-73, 83-95, 104-112, 188-199. Mechanism: _window_start puts the window's first day at batch_day+1 (line 72). window_of gives [start, start+7) with moment = start-1 at make.time (line 93). made_through picks the window whose moment has passed (line 112). due_slots keeps a slot only when slot.local_date < through.end, or when a moved slot's time falls before the horizon (line 198). With batch_day 'wed' the window runs Thu to Wed, so Thu 22 and Fri 23 Oct fall in the window made on Wed 21 Oct. batch_key is the ISO week of the window's first day (76-80): Thu 15 Oct gives 2026-W42, which is why posts dated 19-21 Oct carry W42. The default batch_day is 'sun' (plans.py:44, NEW_PLAN_MAKE plans.py:47), which lines the window up with Mon-Sun.
- F436 objection 6: re-arming the batch 'does nothing', and next_batch_at then advertises a batch that will make nothing. — orchestrator/modules/socials/batches.py:115-123 (with socials_plan_maker.py:392 and api/socials_plans.py:190-195). Mechanism: next_window returns window_of(max(made_through.end, starts_on)) and never checks whether that window is already announced or has any open slot. Plan 945124e6 (Mon/Wed/Fri, batch_day wed, W42 announced 11:27:42) had make.time set to 13:21 at 13:19. At 13:19 the W42 moment (14 Oct 13:21) is in the future, so made_through falls back to [Thu 8, Thu 15). next_window = window_of(max(15 Oct, starts_on 19 Oct)) = the W42 window [15, 22), already announced with both of its slots taken, and plan_view shows next_batch_at 14 Oct 13:21. At 13:21 due_slots is empty (Fri 23 >= 22 Oct, line 198) and nothing touches W42, so _announce_if_complete is never reached (it would return at 392 anyway). next_window then rolls to [22, 29) at 21 Oct. The empty Fri 23 slot is not lost: it is made at the W43 moment.
- F436 objection 5b: a slot moved earlier pre-announces its future week, and that week's real 'Your week is ready' is then never sent. — orchestrator/services/socials_plan_maker.py:229, 407-418, 392 (with batches.py:198). Mechanism: A slot moved before its batch's moment becomes due at once (batches.py:198, 'slot.at < horizon'). claim() stamps batch_key from the slot's original local_date (line 229, plans._slot keeps local_date and changes only 'at'). announce_batches maps touched slot keys to windows by their original day (415-416) and calls _announce_if_complete with no check on window.moment. pending() only sees due_slots(now), so the future week's other slots are not pending, and the week is announced now with a count of 1. At the real moment, _announce_if_complete returns early because the week is already announced (392).
- F436: nothing tells the owner, the slot view or Auto why a slot is empty. A plan in the middle of a build looks the same as a failed one, and the obvious 'derived building' fix would make a stall look like progress (objection 5a). — orchestrator/modules/socials/plan_store.py:187-204; socials_plans.py:190-195; socials_plan_maker.py:135-138, 146-153, 222-237, 334-337; handlers_socials.py:613-633; actions_socials.py:441-485. Mechanism: (1) plan_slots reports only state made|planned (199). It gives no batch, no made_at and no skip reason, although make.batches[key].skipped holds the reasons (batches.skipped_keys). (2) plan_view's next_batch_at rolls forward the moment the batch time passes (batches.py:112). make.batches is written only by _skip (319) and _announce_if_complete (400-401), and there is no current-batch field. (3) Stalls record nothing. _make returns NO_TOPIC after a notice and no per-slot record (334-337). next_topic needs an unused topic that suits the slot's format (topics.py:255-263), so this happens even with unused topics in the bank, and the notice still says 'The content bank is empty' (plan_notify.py:29). With Socials off, _plan_due returns [] (136-138) inside collect_due's read-only session (146-153), so the tick never reaches a slot to record against. Either way the slot stays due and unclaimed. (4) The tick runs every SOCIALS_PLAN_TICK_SECONDS=300 (config.py:2042) on a fixed phase and stamps every topic in a tick with the tick's own 'now' (231). (5) Auto's only plan tool returns a fixed key list (handlers_socials.py:627) plus the whole bank, history and brand_style (628-633). Platform results are dumped as indent=2 JSON (result_formatter.py:876-885) and cut to 2,000 tokens in chat (consumers/chatbot/service.py:90, 1728), so slot rows added there would be cut first. No tool lists plans or reads slots (actions_socials.py:441-485).
- F437: a plan's video draft never got media and records no reason. The render was refused before it started, and the reason was dropped. — orchestrator/services/socials_plan_maker.py:297-312, 341-347, 445 (api/socials.py:568 vs 584; modules/socials/render.py:231-235; service.py:158). Mechanism: write() commits the composer's edit (307, through _commit_unchanged) and the targets (308), then awaits posts_api.render_post (310). render_post builds the bundles at api/socials.py:566-573, before service.start_render at 584. bundle_for raises NotRenderable('fill in item_1_name, … before rendering') when a required variable is empty (render.py:231-233). _make's catch-all (343-347) logs the error, rolls back (the edits are already committed) and sends SLOT_SKIPPED ('A planned post was not made: <plan>: the draft for <topic> waits for you') without the reason, then returns FAILED. The post stays 'draft' with media {} and no review_log entry. The machine has no draft→failed move (ACTION_RENDER_FAILED is {RENDERING: FAILED}, service.py:158). FAILED is also left out of 'touched' (445), so a batch whose last tick only had refusals is never announced. SOC-2 AC2 (same kit) requires this exact refusal to leave the post waiting for the owner, not failed.
- F437 objection 2: every place that shows a render's reason looks only for the 'render_failed' action on a 'failed' post, so a new log action would reach none of them. — frontend/components/deliverables/socials/socials-post-detail.tsx:40-44 (socials-status.ts:18-43; modules/tools/discovery/social_post_list.py:23, 46-51, 58-63; services/social_ticket_post.py:94-115, 168-197). Mechanism: lastRenderFailure returns null unless status === 'failed', then finds the last 'render_failed' entry. D1 (TESTER, code-verified): there is NO off-by-one. A weekly batch makes the 7 local days from the next midnight after batch_day (batches.py window_of), so a slot past that window belongs to the next batch. The faults are: no notice that a slot is outside this batch, a plan mid-build looking failed, a refused plan render dropping its reason, next_batch_at advertising a batch that makes nothing, and a moved slot pre-announcing its week. Ignore the staged AC 'find the off-by-one'.

acceptanceCriteria: Fix step: 0. Before launch (Gerard's call, kit edit). Re-word AC1: 'a slot past the batch's 7 days says which batch makes it and when; a 4-slot week inside one window makes 4 posts'. Do not 'find the off-by-one'. A fixer who extends due_slots past 7 days would make posts under two batch keys and split per-week approval (api/socials_batches.py approves by batch_key). Re-word AC2's 'not left draft': SOC-2 AC2 keeps a post with missing fields waiting, not failed. State in the kit that SOC-2 decides that post's status (draft, or needs_approval 'in review'). SOC-5 builds the shared catch in socials_plan_maker.write/_make, the log entry, the readers and 'touched'. Both stories use ONE log-only action name, proposed 'waiting'. Order SOC-2 before SOC-5 in the wave, or give both write() branches to one fixer (objection 1).

Fix step: 1. Plan render refusal, at socials_plan_maker.py:341-347. Replace the catch-all with _held(db, plan, post, topic, exc), which does: db.rollback(); db.refresh(post); status, h = post.status, post.content_hash. Then: (a) IllegalTransition or StaleContent: another writer has the post (for example the owner already pressed render, so it is RENDERING). Leave it alone; the outcome is TAKEN. A draft-only transition cannot legally move a RENDERING post, and failing it would make render._finish drop the live render (render.py:702). This is a deliberate deviation from the correction's 'IllegalTransition → FAILED'. (b) Platform refusals (render.RendererUnavailable, render_quota.RenderQuotaExceeded, report_charts.ReportUnreadable): service.refuse_render(post, actor, safe) gives DRAFT→FAILED, logged as 'render_failed' so every existing reader shows it. For RendererUnavailable, 'safe' is str(exc) only when it is one of render.STORAGE_MESSAGE, MEDIA_PROFILE_MESSAGE, NOT_CONFIGURED_MESSAGE or UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE, and otherwise UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE. That way render.py:174's f'…not healthy: {exc}' never reaches a notice. The quota and report texts are user-facing constants. Outcome FAILED. (c) Any other SocialsError (NotRenderable including 'fill in …' and NEEDS_PHOTO, ChartNotBindable, ReportNotFound, VoiceUnavailable, InvalidPost): the status stays as SOC-2 decides (draft today), and service.log_waiting(post, actor, str(exc)) is written. These are the texts the route already returns as 422/404 (api/socials.py:269-278). Outcome WAITING. (d) Anything else (compose timeout, LLM error): log_waiting with the fixed text 'The plan could not write this post: write it yourself or ask Auto for another take.', never str(exc). Outcome WAITING. Commit with service.claim_unchanged(db, post, status=status, content_hash=h), else roll back. The notice is a new plan_notify event POST_WAITING = ('social_plan_post_waiting', 'A planned post waits for you: ', 'action_required'), titled '<plan>: <topic>: <why[:200]>'. SLOT_SKIPPED says 'was not made', which is false for a made draft.

Fix step: 7. Why a slot is empty, derived at read time, with stalls separated from building (objection 5a).
